instruments.why: additive harmonic stack -- the general-purpose way to build any harmonic instrument colour: a seven-harmonic gbuzz stack doubled by a twin three cents above, so the pair beats slowly; knh sets how many partials, kmul how fast they fall away
instruments.code:
kad0    poscil 0.0004, 0.053         ; slow drift, upper stack
aa10    gbuzz 0.52, (kfreq * koct1), 7, 1, 0.68, giCos          ; harmonic stack
aa20    gbuzz 0.34, (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0018 + kad0), 7, 1, 0.64, giCos ; twin, +3 cents
asig    = aa10 + aa20
instruments.name: additive

instruments.why: bell / church bell / chime / carillon / tubular bell: true inharmonic bell partials (h 2.76/5.4/8.93) written as 2-operator FM at a 1.41 ratio, so the partials sit off the harmonic grid instead of being projected onto it
instruments.code:

if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  ktm0   = 0
endif

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

instruments.why: three-operator phase modulation: TWO modulators driving one carrier's phase in linear combination, so the spectrum carries two sideband families and the drive travels back and forth BETWEEN them. That travel is what two operators cannot do -- with one modulator a control can only make its single family stronger or weaker, never trade it for a different one. Method: Chowning, JAES 21(7), 1973; the topology and the word-to-parameter directions from Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers on exactly this layout. Csound 6.18 has no generic N-operator opcode, so the two modulators are summed into a `phasor` and read through `tablei`. BJ's reading of the setting this was found at, 2026-07-30: bassoon-like, with a kind of pulse-width modulation -- the `fm` entry beside it reads tine-piano-like. It is NOT a bassoon and does not claim to be one; that reading is what two families trading sounds like at ratio 1.0. DECLARED, and the first thing to know before routing it as a melodic voice: the body transposes exactly with `kfreq`, but WHICH OCTAVE it sounds in is set by `ratio 3`. With `ratio 2` at 1.0 a half-integer `ratio 3` puts the whole spectrum on a grid of `kfreq`/2, so the note sounds an OCTAVE BELOW the key -- measured f0 exactly `kfreq`/2 at 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5 and 6.5, and exactly `kfreq` at 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8, at every register from 55 to 1760 Hz. That subharmonic grid is a setting the axis offers, not the one it ships on: the default is 6.0 and plays the key (+0 ct measured). DECLARED: it STANDS -- the host owns the note-off, so unlike `fm`/`fm_bell`/`metallic_fm` there is no index decay ringing it down (sustain 0.996 to 0.999 across six registers). The spectrum is HARMONIC at every setting: 1.3 to 2.1 % of the energy off the series, measured against the grid the body actually has. An earlier reading of this entry reported 59 to 64 % "off-series" and called the axis an alternation between harmonic and inharmonic -- that was the partials counted against the KEY on a body sounding an octave below it, i.e. the signature of the subharmonic above and not of inharmonicity. What alternates along `ratio 3` is the sounding octave, not the harmonicity. Hayes & Saitis report that on this topology `bright` and `rough` load on the same parameter moves, so a setting cannot be made brighter without also being heard as rougher; that is their finding on their data. Nothing in this repository measures either word, so it is not restated here as a measurement -- reach for this entry for brightness and for two-family movement, and treat roughness as untested. THE MOVEMENT IS IN THE SUSTAIN, and that has to be said because the platform's own movement meter reads the whole note and a spectral attack alone can satisfy it: with the trade frozen this body reads 105 cents over the note and 0 through the sustain, so its onset alone would clear the 60-cent threshold. Running, it reads 748 cents through the sustain at the default (307 to 1405 across the axes). The band is bounded by Carson's rule SUMMED over both operators -- carrier + (I+1)*fm each, both spending the same room -- and the whole drive is scaled by one factor when it does not fit, so the balance between the families and the FRACTION that travels survive the bound. Bounding each operator as if it were alone let the travelling drive arrive on top of an already-full index: at ratio 8/8, both indices 0.6 and `trade` 0.75 on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100 that put a sideband at 49 kHz and 42.7 % of the energy off the grid, against 1.4 % now. The cost of the bound is at the top of the keyboard: above about 880 Hz the drive is scaled down and the body thins toward a sine (centroid 6050 Hz at 880, 5489 at 1760). Two operators on exactly the SAME ratio are one oscillator with a constant total drive and have nothing to trade: unguarded, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so the guard fires only within 0.02 and pushes toward the middle of the range, which reaches 0.7 % of the ratio plane and cannot leave the declared range. The trade oscillator is FREE-RUNNING and the note-on does not reset it, which is the platform's own rule for a loop -- so two notes played minutes apart start at different points in the breath, and the first window's colour differs by up to 375 Hz depending on how long the plugin has been open. Loudness inside a note: 0.01 to 0.19 dB at 220 Hz across all six axes, 0.03 to 0.20 dB at 55 Hz. GATED 2026-07-30 (`tools/lco_axis_probe.py --gate`, 729 corners x 6 registers, at the gate's sr 44100): every corner renders, moves and holds one loudness -- loudness spread 0.03 dB across the corners, 0.0 dB across the registers, 0.03 dB crossed, worst peak 0.66 against the host's 2.52. It reports 339 of 3645 corner-renders away from 220 Hz that do not move, 338 of them at 1760 Hz: at sr 44100 the band ends eleven harmonics above an 1760 Hz note, and two sideband families at high ratios do not fit in it at all, so the band bound scales the drive to nothing. That is the gate's rate, not the instrument's -- re-rendered at the plugin's default 176400 the same corners move 1066 to 1151 cents. Nearest existing entry, and what it was heard against: `fm`.
instruments.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kr2     = 1.00   ; ratio 2[1.0..8.0]: operator 2's tuning ratio -- a whole number is harmonic, between them not
kr3     = 6.00   ; ratio 3[1.0..8.0]: operator 3's ratio, the second family
ki2     = 0.26   ; index 2[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 2 drives, in CYCLES of carrier phase
ki3     = 0.20   ; index 3[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 3 drives
ktrd    = 0.21   ; trade[0.20..0.75]: what FRACTION of the drive travels between the two operators.
                 ;   A fraction and not an amount, so it means the same at any depth: a fixed amount
                 ;   is swamped once both indices are deep. The floor is not zero -- a body always
                 ;   trades a little. The floor is set by the THINNEST body, not by this default:
                 ;   with both indices at zero, 0.10 leaves two ratio settings static and 0.20 does not
kons    = 0.05   ; onset[0.002..0.6]: seconds the sidebands need to arrive -- a SPECTRAL attack
kr3g    = (abs(kr3 - kr2) < 0.02 ? (kr2 > 4.5 ? kr2 - 1.75 : kr2 + 1.75) : kr3)  ; two operators
                                            ;   on exactly the SAME ratio are ONE oscillator with a
                                            ;   constant total drive, so there is nothing to trade:
                                            ;   measured, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the
                                            ;   sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so
                                            ;   only true coincidence is escaped -- and TOWARDS the
                                            ;   middle, so the push cannot leave the declared range
kdrv    = ki2 + ki3 + 0.20                  ; the drive there is to share, plus a floor so a body
                                            ;   with both indices at zero still has something to trade
ktr     = ktrd * kdrv                       ; the amount that travels, before the band is consulted
kpk2    = max(ki2 + ktr, 0.001)             ; what an operator PEAKS at is its own index PLUS all of
kpk3    = max(ki3 + ktr, 0.001)             ;   the travelling drive -- both arrive on one operator
kroom   limit min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc - 1 - kr2 - kr3g, 0, 4000  ; the room the BAND leaves above the two
                                            ;   modulators' first pair. Carson's rule per operator,
                                            ;   summed: (I+1)*fm each, and they spend the SAME room.
                                            ;   Bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put
                                            ;   a 49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3g)   ; radians, so cycles * 2pi
kscl    = min(1, kroom / kneed)              ; one factor for all three, so the balance between the
                                            ;   families and the FRACTION that travels survive it
ki2c    = ki2 * kscl
ki3c    = ki3 * kscl
ktrc    = ktr * kscl
ksw     oscili 0.5, 0.45, giSine            ; free-running, 2.2 s -- more than one cycle in a 3 s note
kt2     = ktrc * (0.5 + ksw)                ; the SAME drive, moving from operator 2 ...
kt3     = ktrc * (0.5 - ksw)                ;   ... to operator 3 and back. Not a level wobble:
karr    = min(knote / kons, 1)              ;   what changes is WHICH family carries the spectrum
am2     poscil (ki2c + kt2) * karr, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil (ki3c + kt3) * karr, kc * kr3g, giSine
aph     phasor kc
apm     = aph + am2 + am3
acar    tablei apm, giSine, 1, 0, 1
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference
asig    balance acar, aref, 10              ; loudness held, colour free. 10 Hz not 1: at a long onset
                                            ;   on a 55 Hz note a 1 Hz follower cannot keep up
asig    = asig * kvol1
instruments.name: 3 op fm

index 2.note: how deep operator 2 drives the carrier, in CYCLES of carrier phase (radians / 2pi). Measured at 220 Hz: centroid 1572 -> 1646 -> 1698 -> 2292 Hz at 0, 0.12, 0.26, 0.6, which is 653 cents against the 2745 that `index 3` covers over the same range -- a quarter of it -- so this is the near family's weight and not the entry's brightness control. At the found `ratio 2` of 1.0 the near family lands on the body's own grid, so what rises with this is harmonic body under the far family. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020 (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator GAIN is what designers raised for `bright` (0.41/0.52, p<.001) and harder still for `rough` (0.63/0.51). Both positive. DECLARED, from the same paper: on FM `bright` and `rough` are very nearly the SAME move, and the authors say why -- "it is challenging to increase the energy in high frequency components without also increasing inharmonicity". This entry can carry `bright` faithfully; it will not separate `rough` from it by these means. Roughness has to come from partials close enough to interact -- a modal bank or a detuned stack -- not from sidebands. WHERE WORDS SIT, from 119,296 human DX7 patches projected onto this entry's two slots (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tool: tools/dx7_corpus.py). Not a listening test and not a meter: it says where a word SITS in the space, never that a rendering earns it. DIRECTION ONLY, as for `index 3`: the DX7's output level is monotone in modulation index but is not a count of cycles. HIGH: clavinet, harpsichord, percussion, jazz guitar, saw. LOW: piccolo, calliope, lute, panflute, chimes, steel drum, clarinet, flute.

bare.gloss: no near family: the far one alone, centroid 1572 Hz

bodied.gloss: the default: body under the far family

packed.gloss: the near family as strong as the far one, 2292 Hz

index 3.note: how deep operator 3 drives -- the brightness axis, and the one that matches Hayes & Saitis's measured direction. Measured at 220 Hz: centroid 792 -> 1208 -> 1698 -> 3149 -> 3865 Hz at 0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60, with the loudness inside a note staying under 0.25 dB. Because `trade` is a fraction of the drive rather than a fixed amount, the movement does not die back as this rises: 477 to 1118 cents through the sustain over the whole axis. WHERE WORDS SIT, from 119,296 human DX7 patches projected onto this entry's two slots (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tool: tools/dx7_corpus.py). Not a listening test and not a meter: it says where a word SITS in the space, never that a rendering earns it. DIRECTION ONLY: the DX7's output level rises with modulation index but does not count cycles, so this is a sign and must never be transcribed as a value. HIGH: clavinet, harpsichord, drums, jazz guitar, saw. LOW: piccolo (the weakest drive in the corpus), clarinet, trumpet, flute, panflute, lute, chimes. `clarinet` is the corpus's sharpest single signature -- 100 % of its voices reach a family at twice the note or beyond, and it drives that family more weakly than any other word. Far and quiet, not far and loud.

dark.gloss: the far family silent; only the near one speaks, 792 Hz

soft.gloss: the far family just audible, 1208 Hz

bright.gloss: the far family carrying the spectrum, 3149 Hz

glaring.gloss: as bright as the band allows, 3865 Hz

ratio 2.note: operator 2's tuning ratio to the carrier -- where the NEAR family sits. Measured at 220 Hz: centroid 1698 -> 1922 -> 2097 -> 3117 Hz at 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 8.0. It does not have to be kept away from `ratio 3`, only off it: a separation of 0.01 already moves 1130 cents through the sustain, while exact coincidence makes the two operators one oscillator with nothing to trade (0 to 9 cents). The guard covers only that coincidence. A ratio is NOT a transposition: a modulator at 2 puts nothing at the octave and one at 3 puts nothing at the twelfth. It decides WHICH partials survive -- at 2 the even ones cancel, at 3 the multiples of three do. The anchors are named for the set that is left. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers steering this exact topology (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator TUNING RATIO is the single largest correlate of `bright` (0.56/0.54, p<.001) and joint-largest of `rough` (0.42/0.56), both POSITIVE -- for either word, raise this. `thick` goes the other way (-0.28, p<.01). Their scope ruling and the full reading: docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §2 and §4.8. WHERE WORDS SIT, from 119,296 human DX7 patches projected onto this entry's two slots (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tool: tools/dx7_corpus.py). Not a listening test and not a meter: it says where a word SITS in the space, never that a rendering earns it. HIGH: mallet and wood block 5.0, bells 3.5, marimba 3.3, vibes 3.0. LOW: the same set as on `ratio 3` -- harpsichord 0.17, oboe and bassoon 0.25, choir and sax 0.5, brass, horn, trombone and string at 1.0.

full series.gloss: the default: every partial present, from the second up. The most ordinary, most pitched setting this entry has

odd only.gloss: the even partials cancel and what is left is 1 3 5 7 9 11 13 ... -- hollow, the colour a square wave has. NOTHING sounds at the octave: a modulator at twice the carrier does not transpose anything, it decides which partials survive

thirds gone.gloss: every partial except the multiples of three: 1 2 4 5 7 8 10 11 ... -- a gapped series, reedier than the full one

odd, far out.gloss: odd only again, but the family reaches to the 35th partial instead of the 25th: thin and glassy, the brightest setting

ratio 3.note: operator 3's tuning ratio -- where the SECOND family sits, and the entry's character control. It sets the sounding OCTAVE as well as the colour, which is the one thing to know about this axis: with `ratio 2` at 1.0, a whole number sounds at the key and a half-integer sounds an octave below it (measured f0 exactly `kfreq`/2 at 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5 and exactly `kfreq` at 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8). The default is 6.0, so it ships at the key; the subharmonic grid is a setting to reach for, not one to arrive on. The spectrum is harmonic either way -- 1.3 to 2.1 % off the series it is actually on. Measured at 220 Hz with `ratio 2` at its default: centroid 920, 1022, 1698, 1977, 2269 Hz at 2.5, 3.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers steering this exact topology (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator TUNING RATIO is the single largest correlate of `bright` (0.56/0.54, p<.001) and joint-largest of `rough` (0.42/0.56), both POSITIVE -- for either word, raise this. `thick` goes the other way (-0.28, p<.01). Their scope ruling and the full reading: docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §2 and §4.8. WHERE WORDS SIT, from 119,296 human DX7 patches projected onto this entry's two slots (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tool: tools/dx7_corpus.py). Not a listening test and not a meter: it says where a word SITS in the space, never that a rendering earns it. HIGH: sitar 7.0, clarinet 6.0, marimba and xylophone 5.0, bells 3.5, vibes 3.0. LOW: harpsichord 0.17, oboe and bassoon 0.25, choir and sax 0.5, and brass, horn, trombone and string all at 1.0 and never above it, even in their upper quartile. `trumpet` and `tuba` go the OTHER way while staying slow, so "brass" is not one place here. Two limits of this axis against that: it stops at 1.0, where the two operators coincide, so the corpus's sub-note family is off its bottom -- BJ's `under` reaches that direction through the half-integer subharmonic at 2.5 instead, and the corpus agrees with his ear on the direction, down. And the corpus's electric pianos sit at 11 to 14 and its acoustic pianos at 20 to 21, above this axis's ceiling of 8.0.

under.gloss: an octave under the key, close family: centroid 920 Hz

at pitch, low.gloss: sounds at the key, close family: 1022 Hz

open.gloss: the default: at the key, the far family, 1698 Hz

high.gloss: at the key, the far family furthest out: 2269 Hz

trade.note: what FRACTION of the drive travels between the two operators. The same total amount is always in play -- what changes is WHICH family carries the spectrum -- so this moves colour and not level: 0.01 to 0.19 dB of loudness travel inside a note at 220 Hz. A fraction and not a fixed amount, because a fixed amount is swamped once both indices are deep: at index 0.6/0.6 a fixed 0.04 left ten corners of the control space static. Through the sustain at 220 Hz: 748, 1171, 1405, 1178 cents at 0.21, 0.35, 0.55, 0.75, with the centroid going 1698 -> 2878 Hz. The floor is set by the THINNEST body and not by this default -- with both indices at zero, 0.10 leaves two ratio settings static and 0.20 does not. Rate 0.45 Hz, 2.2 s, so a 3 s note shows more than one cycle. WHERE WORDS SIT: nowhere. The DX7 has no counterpart to this axis, so the patch corpus in docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7 says nothing about it. This is the entry's own movement and stands on the measurements above alone.

breathing.gloss: the default: 748 cents through the sustain

working.gloss: 1171 cents -- the two families clearly taking turns

churning.gloss: 1405 cents: the spectrum turning inside out and back

restless.gloss: the whole drive changing hands, centroid up to 2878 Hz

onset.note: how long the sidebands take to arrive. A SPECTRAL attack, not a loudness one -- the player owns the amplitude envelope -- and measured, this axis leaves the settled spectrum untouched: centroid 1698 Hz and 748 cents of sustain travel at every value from 0.002 to 0.6. What it changes is how the spectrum gets there, and the arrival counts as colour movement over the note: 748, 747, 1214, 2643 cents at 0.002, 0.05, 0.15, 0.6 measured over the whole note against the 748 that is there in the sustain regardless -- so a short onset adds nothing the sustain does not already have. Hayes & Saitis measured shorter modulator attacks for both bright and rough. WHERE WORDS SIT, from 119,296 human DX7 patches projected onto this entry's two slots (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tool: tools/dx7_corpus.py). Not a listening test and not a meter: it says where a word SITS in the space, never that a rendering earns it. DIRECTION ONLY, and INVERTED -- the DX7's EG rate 1 runs opposite to this axis. SLOW: chimes, organ pipes, violin, choir, and the corpus's whole `/strings` and `/voice` shelves. FAST: percussion, marimba, pizzicato, sitar, synth bass, metal. This is the axis BJ's own reading runs on: `slow` together with `ratio 3` = `under` goes "sehr klar richtung trombone", and the corpus carries both halves of it without having been tuned to -- trombone reaches a far family in 12.6 % of its voices against 40.6 % across the corpus, at attack 57 against 80.

instant.gloss: the full spectrum from the first sample

quick.gloss: the default: the sidebands snap in

eased.gloss: the colour arrives just after the note

slow.gloss: the spectrum opens over more than half a second

kc      = kfreq * koct1

kr3     = 5.50   ; ratio 3[1.0..8.0]: operator 3's ratio, the second family
ki2     = 0.00   ; index 2[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 2 drives, in CYCLES of carrier phase
ki3     = 0.20   ; index 3[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 3 drives
ktrd    = 0.21   ; trade[0.20..0.75]: what FRACTION of the drive travels between the two operators.
                 ;   A fraction and not an amount, so it means the same at any depth: a fixed amount
                 ;   is swamped once both indices are deep. The floor is not zero -- a body always
                 ;   trades a little. The floor is set by the THINNEST body, not by this default:
                 ;   with both indices at zero, 0.10 leaves two ratio settings static and 0.20 does not
kons    = 0.05   ; onset[0.002..0.6]: seconds the sidebands need to arrive -- a SPECTRAL attack
kr3g    = (abs(kr3 - kr2) < 0.02 ? (kr2 > 4.5 ? kr2 - 1.75 : kr2 + 1.75) : kr3)  ; two operators
                                            ;   on exactly the SAME ratio are ONE oscillator with a
                                            ;   constant total drive, so there is nothing to trade:
                                            ;   measured, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the
                                            ;   sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so
                                            ;   only true coincidence is escaped -- and TOWARDS the
                                            ;   middle, so the push cannot leave the declared range
kdrv    = ki2 + ki3 + 0.20                  ; the drive there is to share, plus a floor so a body
                                            ;   with both indices at zero still has something to trade
ktr     = ktrd * kdrv                       ; the amount that travels, before the band is consulted
kpk2    = max(ki2 + ktr, 0.001)             ; what an operator PEAKS at is its own index PLUS all of
kpk3    = max(ki3 + ktr, 0.001)             ;   the travelling drive -- both arrive on one operator
kroom   limit min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc - 1 - kr2 - kr3g, 0, 4000  ; the room the BAND leaves above the two
                                            ;   modulators' first pair. Carson's rule per operator,
                                            ;   summed: (I+1)*fm each, and they spend the SAME room.
                                            ;   Bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put
                                            ;   a 49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3g)   ; radians, so cycles * 2pi
kscl    = min(1, kroom / kneed)              ; one factor for all three, so the balance between the
                                            ;   families and the FRACTION that travels survive it
ki2c    = ki2 * kscl
ki3c    = ki3 * kscl
ktrc    = ktr * kscl
ksw     oscili 0.5, 0.45, giSine            ; free-running, 2.2 s -- more than one cycle in a 3 s note
kt2     = ktrc * (0.5 + ksw)                ; the SAME drive, moving from operator 2 ...
kt3     = ktrc * (0.5 - ksw)                ;   ... to operator 3 and back. Not a level wobble:
karr    = min(knote / kons, 1)              ;   what changes is WHICH family carries the spectrum
am2     poscil (ki2c + kt2) * karr, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil (ki3c + kt3) * karr, kc * kr3g, giSine

acar    tablei apm, giSine, 1, 0, 1
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference

                                            ;   on a 55 Hz note a 1 Hz follower cannot keep up
asig    = asig * kvol1

instruments.why: electric piano -- tine, reed and the FM piano: a struck tine over a body that holds, and a note that falls away while the key is down. The STRUCK reading of frequency modulation -- `fm3` is the held one, and the two name each other the way `plucked_wire` and `string` do. Method: Chowning 1973's percussive construction, the modulation index carrying its own decaying envelope. The tine's ratio, its range and the fact that the far family dies while the near one stands are measured, not recalled: 1386 named electric pianos in the DX7 corpus, docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7. Pre-build record: docs/plans/PLAN_lco_ep_fm3.md. It replaces the struck `fm_ep`, which had every axis this one has except the two that were missing -- the tine's ratio was hardcoded at 14.2 with no knob on it, and the body did not decay at all. NAMED VOICINGS, on BJ's instruction of 2026-07-31 ("biete die klangcharacterista von rhodes I, II, V und wurlitzer etc. an") and corrected the same day on his second one: "ja, korrekt, ABER Du baust ein FM epiano, kein physisches." So the rows are NOT derived from what a real Rhodes pickup does. They are MEASURED from what FM programmers actually did when they wrote these names on a patch -- the DX7 corpus, grouped by the name on the voice (docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §7, tools/dx7_corpus.py --profile). What the corpus separates, and by how much: | name | Stimmen | far ratio | far drive | ratio-2 share | carrier fall | | rhodes/roads | 971 | 14 in 521, then 12, 22, 10 | 71 | 3 % | 99->75 | | suitcase | 24 | 11, 13.5, 13, 12 | 75 | 0 % | 99->75 | | stage | 3 | 14 | 64 | 0 % | 99->75 | | mark 1 / mk 2 / mark iii | 21 | 1 and 14 | 65 | 0 % | 99->93 | | dyno | 157 | 14 in 32 AND 26 in 30 | 80 | 17 % | 99->75 | | wurlitzer | 334 | 14, then 11, 7 | 58 | 41 % | 99->85 | | tine | 99 | 12 in 32, then 14 | 58, and it STAYS (99->85) | 9 % | 99->90 | THREE THINGS THAT MEASUREMENT SAYS AND THE INSTRUMENT WORLD DOES NOT. First, the Mark numbers are not an FM distinction: 21 voices carry one across 119,296, there is no Mark V in the corpus at all, and what the few Mark patches DO share is that they barely decay (carrier 99->93 against everything else's 99->75). What FM programmers separated instead is `dyno` (157) and `suitcase` (24). Second, `dyno` is bimodal on the tine ratio -- 14 in 32 voices and 26 in 30 -- and it is the hottest drive of any group; that second mode is what the name means here. Third, and OPPOSITE to the acoustic instruments: an FM Wurlitzer patch decays LESS than an FM Rhodes patch (99->85 against 99->75), and its separation on this entry is not `tine` at all -- both sit at 14 -- but `hollow`, because 41 % of its modulators sit in the 2-8 band with 198 voices at exactly 2.0, against 3 % for the Rhodes. A modulator at twice the carrier is what cancels the even partials, which is this entry's `hollow` axis by construction. | voicing | tine | ting | ring | hollow | strike | decay | | rhodes | 14 | 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.10 | 0.62 | 0.45 | the corpus's centre of gravity | | rhodes suitcase | 12 | 0.62 | 0.30 | 0.05 | 0.62 | 0.45 | a lower tine and a hotter one | | rhodes stage | 14 | 0.42 | 0.30 | 0.05 | 0.55 | 0.45 | the softest drive of any group | | rhodes mark | 14 | 0.45 | 0.30 | 0.05 | 0.50 | 0.22 | rings on; the one thing the Mark patches share | | dyno | 26 | 0.75 | 0.30 | 0.35 | 0.72 | 0.45 | the second mode and the hottest drive | | wurlitzer | 14 | 0.38 | 0.30 | 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.33 | the even partials cancelled, weakest drive, and it rings LONGER than the Rhodes | | tine | 12 | 0.38 | 0.65 | 0.20 | 0.58 | 0.28 | the far family stays instead of dying | The far-ratio column transfers as a value, since both instruments count it in multiples of the note. The drive and envelope columns are DIRECTIONS only -- the DX7's output level rises with modulation index but does not count cycles, and its EG rate runs the opposite way to `onset`. So the ratios are measured and the other five columns are this entry's reading of a measured direction; BJ's ear decides them. WHAT THE PHYSICAL INSTRUMENTS DO, kept because it explains WHY the FM patches look like this and NOT as the source of any row above: Pfeifle & Muenster, "Tone Production of the Wurlitzer and Rhodes E-Pianos", DAGA 2017 Kiel, 556-559, measured a Rhodes Mark I/II and a Wurlitzer EP200 and found both timbres come from the PICKUP, not the vibrator -- tine and reed both move almost sinusoidally. A Rhodes tine centred on the wedge magnet outputs at TWICE the fundamental, and off centre, or under a larger deflection, the flux change turns asymmetric and the harmonics arrive; the inharmonic part is the brass tonebar and is strongest in the upper register. The Wurlitzer's reed has negligible higher modes, so its harmonics come from the reed's non-symmetric design changing the capacitance differently on each excursion -- the bark. That is why an FM Wurlitzer is built from a low-order modulator and an FM Rhodes from a high one. WHAT THESE ROWS DO NOT CARRY: the amplifier and the effects. The cased instrument is a tremolo, the stage instrument through a phase-shifter pedal is a phaser, and the bark is an overdrive -- none of that is in this body. THE EFFECTS ARE KNOBS ON THE SYNTH, NOT LINES IN THIS BODY. Wired 2026-07-31 on BJ's instruction ("Was fehlt sind Effekte ... verzerrung, tremolo, chorus, phaser"), they sit in the amplifier behind the voices, which is what these instruments' effects ARE: the cased instrument has ONE tremolo for the whole instrument, not one per key. Reach them with SET lines and never with Csound -- `fx_trem_rate` / `fx_trem_depth` / `fx_trem_stereo`, `fx_chorus_rate` / `fx_chorus_depth` / `fx_chorus_mix`, `fx_phaser_rate` / `fx_phaser_depth` / `fx_phaser_feedback` / `fx_phaser_mix`, `fx_dist_drive` / `fx_dist_mix`. All four are OFF at their defaults, so a prompt that does not ask for one gets none. TWO WORDS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE LAND IN THE WRONG PLACE: `tremolo` is also a movement in this library and `distorted` also a sound word, and both of those write into the BODY. Alongside this entry they belong on the knobs above -- a per-voice tremolo beats against itself the moment two keys are held, and this body's own drive is already its `strike` axis. WHERE THE NAMED VOICINGS PUT THEM: the cased voicing = a stereo PAN, because that instrument's vibrato pans between its two amplifier pairs, so `fx_trem_stereo` near 1 with a rate around 5 Hz; the reed voicing = an AMPLITUDE tremolo from its one amplifier, `fx_trem_stereo` 0; the stage voicing through a phase-shifter pedal = `fx_phaser_*` slow, rate under 0.5; the bright-chorused voicing = chorus. THE BARK IS NOT ON THIS LIST and must not be routed here -- BJ heard two attempts on 2026-07-31 and ruled it out: "es klingt nicht ab. das ist ein 4-sekunden-bark. ein bark bei einem epiano klingt aber nach hoechstens 1 sek ab ... das bark-Sample hat keine Transiente, die wird verschluckt." Measured, the amplifier cut the attack contrast from the dry body's +6.8 dB to +5.3 and its excess over that body GREW across the note (+3.9 to +5.0 dB) rather than dying. The corpus says why, over 842 named e-pianos: the far modulator -- the bright, barking part -- falls at envelope rate 50 where the carrier falls at 25, so the bark carries its OWN envelope at about twice the speed of the note. A stage behind the voices has no envelope; it follows the level, and the level falls more slowly than the modulation. So the bark is `strike` on THIS entry, in the body, and never `fx_dist_*`. Those five are starting points for the ear and NOT measurements -- the corpus above measures the patch, and a pedal in front of an amplifier leaves no trace in a DX7 voice.
instruments.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: decay
; Struck once and then falling away while the key is held, the way an electric piano
; does -- the player's envelope cannot hold it up. The STANDING reading of this body is
; `fm3`: a prompt that wants a held two-modulator FM tone belongs there, not here.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
ktine   = 14.0   ; tine[6.0..28.0]: where the metal of the strike stands, as a multiple of
                 ;   the note. Measured over 1386 named electric pianos in the DX7 corpus:
                 ;   14 is the mode (595 voices) and 10, 12, 18, 22, 26, 28 all occur
kting   = 0.55   ; ting[0.0..1.0]: how much of the strike is that metal
kring   = 0.30   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the metal takes to die back into the body
khol    = 0.55   ; hollow[0.0..1.0]: the body's harmonics, full series to odd only
kstr    = 0.64   ; strike[0.0..1.0]: how bright the body starts before it softens
kdec    = 0.45   ; decay[0.0..1.0]: how fast the whole note falls away
; --- Chowning 1973 (JAES 21(7), 526-534) builds a struck tone by giving the modulation
;     INDEX its own decaying envelope, so the spectrum darkens as the note falls instead
;     of being filtered down. Both envelopes below are that, and the corpus says how the
;     two differ: a DX7 electric piano's FAR modulator dies back (envelope level 99 -> 75)
;     while its NEAR one stands (99 -> 93). So the body softens and then holds; the metal
;     goes away entirely.
ktau    = 0.08 + 1.40 * kring * kring                ; the tine's time constant, seconds
ktfd    = exp(-knote / ktau)                         ; and the one shape it decays on
kbdx    = (1.302 + 2.898 * kstr) * (0.60 + 0.40 * exp(-knote / 1.10))
; --- 0.60 and not 0.29 is the corpus's own number and it is load-bearing twice over. A
;     `foscili` at a carrier:modulator ratio of 1:1 or 1:2 has sidebands that fold through
;     DC and interfere with the upper ones, so its LEVEL is a function of its index -- at
;     amp 0.30 and 220 Hz, 1:1 measures +0.24, -0.43, -2.88, -1.49, +0.01 dB against a
;     sine at index 0.5, 0.9, 1.5, 3.2, 4.2. An index envelope on such a pair is therefore
;     also an amplitude envelope, and with the old 3.4x swing the whole body SWELLED
;     4.55 dB over the first 1.3 s at `decay` 0 / `hollow` 0.25 / `ting` 0, which
;     `; DECAY: SELF` does not cover and `--gate` does not catch (its swell candidate is a
;     linear fit from t = 1 s and reads the later decay as a fall). The corpus fixes the
;     depth without a fitted number: its NEAR modulators fall only from envelope level 99
;     to 93 over the note while the far ones fall to 75, which is where the settle belongs.
; --- 1.302..4.200 is `fm_ep`'s own index range, kept rather than re-chosen. Lowering
;     the floor to 0.8 left the body at index 0.23 once it had settled -- near enough
;     to a bare sine that `lco_axis_probe --gate` failed 27 corners for not moving,
;     all of them at `strike` 0 with `ting` 0. The old entry's floor is the capability
;     this one has to preserve, not a number to improve on.
ktng    = 3.0 * kting * ktfd
; --- the tine's LEVEL falls on that same shape and not only its index, because an index
;     falling to zero does not remove an operator pair -- it turns the pair into a bare
;     sine ON the note, which then adds in phase with the body. Measured before this line
;     existed: the whole body SWELLED 1.5 dB over the first half second and only fell
;     after, which `; DECAY: SELF` does not cover (`declares_decay` passes a fall and
;     fails a swell). The corpus has it right: its algorithm 5 gives every carrier its own
;     envelope, so the modulator's level cuts the index and the carrier's cuts the pair.
; --- Nyquist, Carson's rule PER PAIR. These are three separate carriers with one
;     modulator each, so each pair's deviation is its own -- unlike `fm3` and
;     `metallic_fm`, where two modulators arrive on ONE carrier phase and the room has to
;     be shared. What is reserved is what an operator can EVER ask for, never what it is
;     asking for now: a guard that divides by the live index divides the envelope and the
;     axis straight back out, and `metallic_fm` records three `ring` settings rendering
;     BIT-IDENTICAL from exactly that mistake.
kband   limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc) - 1, 2, 4000  ; room above the carrier, in notes
ktr     limit ktine, 1, max(kband, 1)                ; the tine cannot stand above the band
; --- capped at the band and not at half of it. Half reserved room for the tine to keep an
;     index of 1, which `ksct` below already handles on its own -- and the cost was the
;     axis: measured, `tine` 14, 22 and 28 rendered IDENTICALLY from 880 Hz and the whole
;     declared range collapsed to one sound from 1530 Hz. That is the exact fault this
;     body's own guard comment cites against `metallic_fm`, left in the entry's headline
;     axis. At the band the collapse starts at about 2860 Hz instead, which is where the
;     physics really puts it: a 28th partial of 2860 Hz is 80 kHz and no reserve invents it.
kscb    = min(1, max(kband / 2 - 1, 0) / 4.2)        ; 4.200 = kbdx at the strike, `strike` 1
ksct    = min(1, max(kband / ktr - 1, 0) / 3.0)      ; 3.0 = ktng at the strike, `ting` 1
; --- three carriers on the note, which is the shape the corpus's own algorithm 5 has in
;     854 of those 1386 voices. `hollow` is a LEVEL crossfade and never a ratio sweep: a
;     modulator ratio swept from 1 to 2 passes through 1.5, and `fm3`'s `ratio 3` measures
;     what that does -- the note drops an octave. Equal power on both crossfades, so they
;     move colour and not level.
aevn    foscili 0.30, kc, 1, 1, kbdx * kscb, giSine    ; body, the full series
aodd    foscili 0.30, kc, 1, 2, kbdx * kscb, giSine, 0.25   ; body, even partials cancelled
; --- the quarter cycle on `aodd` is not a tuned number, it is QUADRATURE. Both body pairs
;     run on the same carrier, the same table and, without it, the same start phase, so
;     their fundamentals add IN PHASE and the sum is louder in the middle of `hollow` than
;     at either end -- and because a `foscili` at these ratios has a level that follows its
;     index (see above), that coherent sum is also a level that MOVES as `kbdx` decays.
;     Measured with both at phase 0: the body swelled 2.87 dB at `hollow` 0.25 while
;     `hollow` 0 and 1, each a single carrier, swelled 0.00. A quarter cycle puts the two
;     in quadrature at the note, where the sum is the power sum whatever the index does.
atin    foscili 0.30, kc, 1, ktr, ktng * ksct, giSine  ; the tine
abod    = aevn * sqrt(1 - khol) + aodd * sqrt(khol)
; --- body and tine are ONE equal-power crossfade whose position is the strike itself:
;     `ting` says how far it travels, `ktfd` brings it home. The hammer's energy goes into
;     the metal at the strike and comes back to the body as the metal dies, so the tine
;     LEAVES rather than thinning into a sine on the note -- and because the two sides are
;     complementary the sum's power is flat, which leaves `exp(-knote / ktaud)` as the only
;     amplitude shape in the body and therefore the only thing `; DECAY: SELF` has to
;     cover. Both other constructions were rendered and rejected on measurement, not
;     taste: with the tine merely losing its index the whole body SWELLED 1.5 dB before it
;     fell (a bare sine on the note, adding in phase with the body), and with the body
;     ducked for the whole note instead of for the strike `ting` cost 5.2 dB across its
;     own range -- a colour control behaving as a volume control, which
;     docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md §4 requires to stay catchable.
kmix    = kting * ktfd
asum    = abod * sqrt(1 - kmix) + atin * sqrt(kmix)
; --- NO level follower anywhere in this body, on purpose. `fm_ep` held its loudness with
;     `balance ..., 10`, and a 10 Hz corner tracks and FLATTENS everything slower than
;     itself -- a tine decaying with a 0.21 s constant is 4.8 Hz, so the strike was being
;     levelled out by the body's own loudness guard. That is what BJ heard as "eintoenig
;     und schlicht" (2026-07-31). Moving the corner does not repair it: at `ring` = 1 the
;     tine's constant is 1.5 s, which is under 1 Hz as well. It is not needed either --
;     frequency modulation redistributes power rather than adding it, and both crossfades
;     above are equal-power, so the level holds across every axis without a follower.
ktaud   = 0.30 + 11.0 * (1 - kdec) * (1 - kdec)       ; seconds
asig    = asum * exp(-knote / ktaud) * kvol1

instruments.curated: BJ, 2026-07-31: abgenommen. Seine Worte zu diesem Eintrag: „ep_fm hat ja funktioniert, war nur eintönig und schlicht, 90 Jahre niveau. aber eine Basis.“ | „nimm die neuen erkenntnisse und baue also ein ep_fm3 oder epiano als parameter im fm3“ | „ok, ep_fm3 funktioniert gut, hiermit abgenommen.“ — gehört über tools/lco_listening/ep_fm3_params/index.html, also über eine Seite mit sichtbarer und wählbarer Parameterkombination, und gegen tools/lco_listening/ep_fm3_ab/ mit `metallic_fm` als nächstem Bibliothekseintrag (gerendert VOR der ersten Orchesterzeile) und drei SA3-Referenzen auf „solo electric piano". Vorab-Aufzeichnung mit Verfahren und Quelle: docs/plans/PLAN_lco_ep_fm3.md. Die Abnahme gilt dem Klang; die beiden hier vermerkten Defekte (Schwellen bei langem `decay`, `tine` tot über ~2860 Hz) sind damit NICHT abgenommen und bleiben offen.

tine.note: where the metal of the strike stands, as a multiple of the note. THIS IS THE AXIS `fm_ep` DID NOT HAVE: it hardcoded 14.2 and put no control on it, which is the defect docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §4.8 records for the old `fm` -- "what the designers reached for hardest has no knob here". Hayes & Saitis 2020 measured the modulator tuning ratio as the single largest correlate of `bright` (0.56/0.54, p<.001) over thirty sound designers on this topology, so raising this is their measured direction for that word. The RANGE is the corpus's own: over 1386 named electric pianos 14 is the mode with 595 voices, and 10, 12, 18, 22, 26 and 28 all occur -- the tine is a range and not a number. DECLARED, and measured rather than softened: this axis DIES at the top of the keyboard, because a 28th partial of 2860 Hz is 80 kHz and no reserve invents it. Five values of this axis rendered at one pitch come back as 5 different sounds at 220 Hz, 4 at 880, 3 at 1530, 2 at 2000 and ONE from about 2860 Hz up -- above that the entry has five axes, not six.

close metal.gloss: the metal sits near the body, more thud than ting

tine.gloss: the corpus's own most common tine, 595 of 1386 voices

high tine.gloss: thin and glassy, well clear of the body

needle.gloss: the top of the corpus's range; only low notes carry it

ting.note: how much of the strike is metal. This is the single feature that separates an electric piano from a plain FM tone; at 0 the instrument is only its body. The metal fades back out of the tone as the note is held -- it loses its brightness, and it trades against the body rather than being added on top, so this moves colour and not level. Hayes & Saitis measured the modulator GAIN rising for both `bright` (0.41/0.52) and `rough` (0.63/0.51).

none.gloss: the body alone, no metal in the strike

classic.gloss: the default: a struck electric piano

clangy.gloss: the metal is most of the attack

ring.note: how long the metal takes to die back into the body -- the tine's time constant, 0.08 s at the bottom and 1.48 s at the top. Short is a quick struck-tine click, long is a metallic buzz that stays through most of the note. Both ends are the corpus's: its far modulators fall from envelope level 99 to 75 at rate 50, which is quick, but the rate varies across the 1386 voices. This is the tine's OWN decay and not the note's -- that is `decay`.

click.gloss: the metal is gone in a third of a second

medium.gloss: the metal carries into the note

long.gloss: a wurlitzer-like reed that buzzes on

hollow.note: the body's harmonics, from the full series to odd only. Low keeps every harmonic and sounds broad and piano-like; high cancels the even ones, which is what makes a reed sound hollow and nasal. It is a LEVEL crossfade between two bodies and never a ratio sweep: a modulator ratio swept from 1 to 2 passes through 1.5, and `fm3`'s `ratio 3` measures what that does -- the note drops an octave. Equal power, so it moves colour and not level.

strike.note: how bright the body starts before it softens. This shapes the tone and not the volume -- a hard strike is brighter, not louder, because frequency modulation redistributes power rather than adding it. The body settles to 29 % of its opening index over about a second and then HOLDS there, which is the corpus's near modulator: envelope level 99 falling only to 93 while the far one falls to 75.

soft.gloss: barely struck, almost a sine body

hard.gloss: the body opens bright and closes down over a second

decay.note: how fast the whole note falls away while the key is held: a time constant of 11.3 s at the bottom and 0.30 s at the top. This is the axis `fm_ep` did not have at all -- docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md §4 records that `fm_ep` emitted no amplitude envelope and was the STANDING reading of an instrument whose whole character is that it falls away, and that "the convention's other half -- the real instrument, with its own decay -- does not exist at all". The body declares `; DECAY: SELF` and the player's envelope cannot hold the note up. A prompt that wants a held FM tone belongs in `fm3`. The corpus's carriers decay too, from envelope level 99 to 75.

clipped.gloss: a third of a second; struck and gone

instruments.name: drum

pitched.note: how definite the pitch is. an ideal stretched membrane rings at spacings that are not whole-number multiples, so it has no clear note -- that is a tom. loading the head with air in a kettle pulls those spacings towards whole numbers until a real pitch appears -- that is a timpani. this is the deepest thing about the instrument, not a tuning offset: the played pitch itself never changes here, only whether the drum sounds like it HAS one.

tom.gloss: no clear note, just a low woody thump

mixed.gloss: a note starts to emerge from the thump

timpani.gloss: a real singing pitch, a tuned kettledrum

strikepos.note: where the head is struck. dead centre wakes only the modes that breathe evenly across the whole skin, which is round and deep; nearer the rim wakes the ones that ripple around it, which is thinner, harder and more sharply coloured. a real player uses this constantly.

tension.note: how tightly the head is stretched, heard as which partials carry the sound rather than as pitch. slack leaves only the lowest ones and sounds dull and floppy; tight brings the upper ones up and sounds bright and taut.

damping.note: how freely the head is allowed to ring, as with a hand or a felt ring on the skin. open leaves narrow clear resonances that sing; muffled broadens them until the drum reads as a thud with a colour rather than a tone.

muffled.gloss: dead and thuddy, a cloth on the skin

instruments.why: gong / tam-tam / anvil / metallic percussion (a singing bowl is `singing_bowl`, a different body with a definite pitch): two phase-modulation operators standing on the (3,0) and (4,0) modes Chladni's law predicts for a free circular plate, driving one carrier and a second carrier a few Hz above it. The exponent of that law is the instrument's main axis, so the metal runs from a tight nearly-pitched body to a wide plate with no note left; each mode has its own decay, so the attack is bright and the tail is not. Since the migration to three operators this entry has the topology Hayes & Saitis 2020 measured -- two modulators in linear combination on ONE carrier's phase -- so under BJ's scope ruling of 2026-07-29 (that source concerns FM entries only) their word-to-parameter directions now apply here as they do to `fm3`: `index` is their modulator gain, `stretch` sets both their tuning ratios. Before the migration it was `foscili` with the ratio hardcoded at 2.41 and no knob on it at all, which is what docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §4.8 records as "what the designers reached for hardest has no knob here".
instruments.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kidx    = 0.53   ; index[0.0..1.0]: how hard the two modes are driven -- how many partials the
                 ;   metal carries, and how far the pitch of the note loosens
kstr    = 1.70   ; stretch[1.40..2.40]: Chladni's exponent p in f = C(m+2n)^p. The published
                 ;   range for cymbals, handbells and church bells; about 2 is a flat circular
                 ;   plate, the gong end. Low is a tight, nearly-pitched metal
kring   = 0.56   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the drive holds before the metal darkens
kdmp    = 0.35   ; damping[0.0..1.0]: how much faster the upper mode dies than the lower one
; LOUDNESS: beat
kbeat   = 0.50   ; beat[0.0..1.0]: how fast the two struck bodies swell against each other
; --- the two ratios are COMPUTED from the law, not chosen. Modes (2,0) (3,0) (4,0) of a
;     free circular plate have (m+2n) = 2, 3, 4, so f_k / f_2 = (k/2)^p
kr2     = pow(1.5, kstr)         ; operator 2 stands ON the (3,0) mode
kr3     = pow(2.0, kstr)         ; operator 3 stands ON the (4,0) mode
; --- Kirchhoff's plate equation carries TWO loss terms (Schaefer, Werner & Rabenstein,
;     "Physical Modeling of Vibrating Plates", DAGA 2019 Rostock, 299-302, eq. 1). d1 is
;     frequency-independent and "leads to a uniform damping for all oscillation modes" --
;     that is `ring`. d3 scales with the squared wavenumber, and since the squared
;     wavenumber goes with the mode's FREQUENCY (eq. 15), the decay rate of eq. 14 is
;     affine in the mode ratio: the higher a mode stands, the faster it dies. d3 is
;     `damping`. A held note keeps driving the plate, and a driven damped mode settles at
;     drive/rate -- so a mode that dies q times faster also STANDS q times lower. That is
;     the steady state of the same equation, not a number fitted to a result.
ktau    = 0.15 + 6.0 * kring * kring
kd3     = 3.0 * kdmp * kdmp
kq2     = 1 + kd3 * (kr2 - 1)               ; mode (3,0) decays this many times faster
kq3     = 1 + kd3 * (kr3 - 1)               ; mode (4,0), standing higher, faster still
kf2     = 0.30 / kq2                        ; and sits that much lower while driven
kf3     = 0.30 / kq3
kenv2   = kf2 + (1 - kf2) * exp(-knote * kq2 / ktau)
kenv3   = kf3 + (1 - kf3) * exp(-knote * kq3 / ktau)
ksw     oscili 0.30, 0.31, giSine   ; slow, free-running: which mode carries the metal
ki2     = kidx * 0.60 * kenv2 * (1 - ksw)
ki3     = kidx * 0.42 * kenv3 * (1 + ksw)
; --- Nyquist, Carson's rule per operator and summed -- both modulators arrive on ONE carrier
;     phase, so the deviation that counts is their SUM and the room is shared. `fm3` records
;     what happens otherwise: "bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put a
;     49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note". What is reserved is what an operator
;     can EVER ask for -- `index` at the top of its range, envelope at 1, ksw at its peak --
;     never what it is asking for right now. A guard that divides by the live index divides
;     the envelope and the axis straight back out: every common factor of ki2 and ki3
;     cancels against kneed, and where the guard bites, `ring`, `damping` and `index` stop
;     doing anything at all. Measured 2026-07-31 before this line was written: at 1760 Hz,
;     stretch 2.4, damping 0, three `ring` settings rendered BIT-IDENTICAL and moves() went
;     False. `fm3` already reserves from an operator's peak for this reason. kroom has a
;     FLOOR and not a zero, because a body whose room reaches zero is a bare sine with every
;     axis dead. DECLARED LIMIT, measured 2026-07-31 and shared with `fm3`: the 20000 ceiling
;     dates from when the page and the plugin still ran at 1x, and against it this pot is
;     already at its floor by A7 -- at 3520 Hz the body is close to a sine and its colour
;     travels 9 Hz, under the movement gate. Every register up to and including A6 moves.
kpk2    = 0.60 * 1.30
kpk3    = 0.42 * 1.30
kroom   limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc) - 1 - kr2 - kr3, 0.5, 4000
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3)
kscl    = min(1, kroom / max(kneed, 0.001))  ; one factor for both, so their balance holds
ki2s    = ki2 * kscl
ki3s    = ki3 * kscl
; --- two modulators on one carrier's phase, and a second carrier a few Hz above, so the
;     pair beats the way two struck metal bodies do
am2     poscil ki2s, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil ki3s, kc * kr3, giSine
kbea    = 0.5 * kbeat           ; Hz, so the SLOWEST partial beats at kbea and the
                                ;   n-th at n*kbea -- which is why this has to stay well
                                ;   under 1 Hz: at 1.3 Hz the third partial beat 3.9 times
                                ;   a second and BJ heard it as hectic (2026-07-31)
acr1    tablei (phasor:a(kc)) + am2 + am3, giSine, 1, 0, 1
acr2    tablei (phasor:a(kc + kbea)) + am2 + am3, giSine, 1, 0, 1
asum    = acr1 * 0.60 + acr2 * 0.40
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference
; The level stage sees ONE voice, not the pair. A follower fast enough for the spectral
; onset (10 Hz) is by definition fast enough to FLATTEN a beat slower than that, and at
; ihp=1 it still swallows anything under a Hz -- docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md l.173 records that
; `fm_bell`'s ihp=1 "exists to protect its doublet beat", and this body's beat is slower
; than either follower. Taking the gain from the first voice alone holds the loudness and
; leaves the beat in. Measured: 2.4 dB of swell before, 14.8 dB after, at the rate asked for
krms1   rms acr1, 10
krmsr   rms aref, 10
kg      = krmsr / (krms1 + 0.0001)
asig    = asum * kg
asig    = asig * kvol1
instruments.name: metal

stretch.note: how far the metal's modes stand off a harmonic series. This is not a free number: it is the exponent p of Chladni's law, f = C(m+2n)^p, and the two operators are placed at the (3,0) and (4,0) modes it predicts. The range is the published one for cymbals, handbells and church bells. Low is a tight metal that still carries the note; high is a wide plate whose partials no longer add up to a pitch. It is ALSO the two modulator tuning ratios at once, because the law computes them from p. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers steering this exact topology (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator TUNING RATIO is the single largest correlate of `bright` (0.56/0.54, p<.001) and joint-largest of `rough` (0.42/0.56), both POSITIVE -- for either word, raise this. `thick` goes the other way (-0.28, p<.01). Their scope ruling and the full reading: docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §2 and §4.8.

tight.gloss: the modes closest together: a small, nearly-pitched metal

bell.gloss: the middle of the published range: struck bell, the note still there

plate.gloss: a flat circular plate, the value the law gives for one: gong

wide.gloss: the top of the published range: the partials furthest apart, no note left

index.note: how hard the two modes are driven -- how many partials the metal carries. Low leaves the note almost bare; high fills the spectrum between the modes and loosens the pitch, because a deep index empties the carrier itself. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020 (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator GAIN is what designers raised for `bright` (0.41/0.52, p<.001) and harder still for `rough` (0.63/0.51). Both positive. DECLARED, from the same paper: on FM `bright` and `rough` are very nearly the SAME move, and the authors say why -- "it is challenging to increase the energy in high frequency components without also increasing inharmonicity". This entry can carry `bright` faithfully; it will not separate `rough` from it by these means. Roughness has to come from partials close enough to interact -- a modal bank or a detuned stack -- not from sidebands.

struck softly.gloss: barely driven: the note with a trace of metal on it

struck.gloss: an ordinary strike, the modes clearly there

struck hard.gloss: hard: the spectrum fills in between the modes

hammered.gloss: hammered, the pitch beginning to loosen

crashed.gloss: everything the two modes can put out

damping.note: how much faster a mode dies for standing higher. Kirchhoff's plate equation has two loss terms: one that damps every mode alike -- that is `ring` -- and one that grows with the mode's frequency. This is the second one. At zero the metal is damped evenly and keeps its colour for as long as the note lasts; turned up, the modes the law puts furthest out go first, and what is left is the plain low body. A held note keeps driving the plate, so a mode that dies faster also stands lower the whole way through -- this is not only an attack shape.

even.gloss: no frequency-dependent loss at all: every mode falls at the same rate and the metal holds its colour to the end of the note

metal.gloss: the default: the (4,0) mode dies about twice as fast as the body and stands about half as high -- an ordinary struck metal

dead top.gloss: the top is gone in a fifth of the time and sits 20 dB down: the low body alone, still ringing

ring.note: how long the drive holds before the metal darkens. Low collapses to a plain body almost at once; high stays lit deep into the note. The host owns when the note stops -- this is the colour, not the loudness.

quick.gloss: the metal darkens almost at once

long.gloss: stays lit well into the note

beat.note: how fast the two struck bodies swell against each other. NOT a detune: the offset is a fraction of a Hertz and you never hear it as pitch, you hear the two bodies going in and out of step -- BJ, 2026-07-31, on the name it used to carry: „das ist kein detune“. The swell has to be SLOW: the n-th partial swells n times as fast as the first, so an offset near 1 Hz makes the third partial pulse almost four times a second, which he heard as hectic. The whole axis stays under 0.5 Hz. At zero the two lock and the body stands still -- the static escape, and about 2.7 dB louder, because two bodies in step add where two bodies beating do not.

locked.gloss: the two bodies in step: one still body, and the loudest setting

slow.gloss: 0.2 Hz: one swell every five seconds

wide.gloss: 0.43 Hz: the fastest swell this body offers

instruments.why:
singing bowl / Klangschale / Tibetan bowl: a bank of `mode` resonators on the (j,0) modes of an axisymmetric shell, every mode a PAIR split by a measured fraction, struck by a mallet or rubbed into a mode lock-in. It exists because `metallic_fm` -- a Chladni free circular plate, and a good gong -- is the wrong body for the word, and the mismatch is objective rather than a matter of taste: that entry computes its two ratios from Chladni's law as 1.5^p and 2.0^p over a declared p of [1.4, 2.4], and a bowl's first two overtones at 2.83 and 5.42 would need p = 2.57 for the one operator and 2.44 for the other -- two different exponents, both outside the range. Rendered at its defaults at 220 Hz its loudest low partial sits at 62 Hz: it does not carry the note. BJ, 2026-07-29: „Crystal singing bowls in a cathedral“ comes out extremely dissonant, „Wäre gut da eine eigene Parametrisierung zu machen (oder Instrument)“.

THE POINT OF THE BODY, in the source's own sentence: ‚The frequency relationships are mildly inharmonic, which does not affect the definite pitch of this instrument, mainly dominated by the first (2,0) shell mode.‘ A bowl has a DEFINITE PITCH. That is exactly what a gong does not have and exactly what was missing.

SOURCES, both read in full, both quoted in docs/plans/PLAN_lco_singing_bowl.md with their tables: Inácio, Henrique & Antunes, ‚The dynamics of Tibetan singing bowls‘, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 92 (2006) 637-653 -- experimental modal identification of four bowls, which supplies the mode series, the pair splits and the damping range; and Terwagne & Bush, ‚Tibetan singing bowls‘, arXiv:1106.6348 -- the closed form f(j,0) ~ j(j^2-1)/sqrt(j^2+1), the finding that only (n,0) modes are excited at all, and the rubbed mode lock-in that `sung` runs on. Nothing here is fitted: the two ends of the main axis are two bowls somebody measured.

DECLARED PROPERTIES, because an author has to be able to route this without hearing it first. It FOLLOWS `kfreq` -- the whole bank stands on kc, and the (2,0) mode is the note. It DECAYS (`; DECAY: SELF`): struck, it rings down on its own, and at the long end of `ring` that ring-down is far longer than any note this instrument plays -- Q 5228 at the default is a 1/e time of 7.6 s -- so inside a 0.1-11 s note it is a standing tone that darkens. Rubbed (`sung` 1.0) it stands outright, which is what a rubbed bowl does.

WHAT IT MEASURES AND IS NOT: it is FLAT ACROSS THE KEYBOARD, which was not true before the exciter was repaired and is worth stating because of that. At the attack: 110 +4.73, 220 +2.99, 440 +0.40, 880 +4.50 dB -- 4.34 dB of spread and -0.08 dB per octave, i.e. scatter and not a slope. `mode`'s gain at resonance does go with Q over frequency, and the library's other mode banks show it (`driven_metal` -2.72, `drum_head` -2.99 dB/octave); here the strike is broadband enough that it does not read as a tilt. What DOES stay over the one-loudness bound is the corner space: 8.01 dB across the 81 corners at 220 Hz and 12.67 dB across corners and registers together, and most of that is `sung`, whose two halves are one strike and no strike. Declared, not flattened. Post-onset peak at the rate the plugin runs Csound (176400 -- `lroOsFactor_` is 4 in PluginProcessor.h, capped at 200 kHz), with the instance old enough that none of the build-time strike is left: 0.76 at 220 Hz at the defaults, and 2.20 at the loudest corner the body has -- 110 Hz, `ring` free, `warble` at its narrowest -- against a clip ceiling of 2.52 transparent and 2.75 absolute. So it clips nowhere, and it is quieter at its defaults than the library's other mode banks are at theirs (`struck_bar` 1.96, `cymbal` 2.26). That is the price of a corner space this wide and it is declared rather than hidden.
instruments.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: warble
; A Tibetan singing bowl as what the measurements say it is: an axisymmetric shell whose
; (j,0) modes are MILDLY inharmonic and therefore keep a definite pitch -- Inacio, Henrique
; & Antunes, Acta Acustica 92 (2006) 637-653, on four bowls they identified experimentally.
; That is the whole difference to `metallic_fm`, which is a Chladni plate and has no pitch.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kbowl   = 0.50   ; bowl[0.0..1.0]: which measured bowl the mode series is
kwarb   = 0.30   ; warble[0.0..1.0]: how far the two halves of each mode pair stand apart
kring   = 0.60   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the shell holds
ksung   = 0.00   ; sung[0.0..1.0]: struck (shell modes) -> rubbed (mode lock-in, harmonics)
; --- THE MODE SERIES. Two MEASURED bowls, not a curve through them: Bowl 2 (563 g, 152 mm)
;     is the flattest of the four and Bowl 4 the widest, and Bowl 4 sits almost exactly on
;     the in-plane ring solution f_j ~ j(j^2-1)/sqrt(j^2+1) that Terwagne & Bush validate
;     for j = 2..6 (arXiv:1106.6348 Eq. 5). `bowl` travels between the two, so every
;     position is between two real instruments.
kr2     = 1.0
kr3     = 2.70 + 0.20 * kbowl      ; Bowl 2: 2.7   Bowl 4: 2.9
kr4     = 4.80 + 0.90 * kbowl      ;         4.8          5.7
kr5     = 7.50 + 1.60 * kbowl      ;         7.5          9.1
kr6     = 10.60 + 2.50 * kbowl     ;        10.6         13.1
kr7     = 14.20 + 3.50 * kbowl     ;        14.2         17.7
; --- DAMPING. zeta 0.002..0.015 % measured, "higher values pertaining to higher-order
;     modes", and "may increase one order of magnitude, or more, depending on how the bowls
;     are actually supported or handled". Q = 1/(2*zeta): 25000 free, ~330 held. `ring` runs
;     that span; the per-mode factor is the paper's own direction and not a fitted number.
kz      = 0.00002 * exp(log(50.0) * (1 - kring))   ; 0.002 % .. 0.1 %
kq2     = 1 / (2 * kz)
kq3     = kq2 / 1.30
kq4     = kq2 / 1.70
kq5     = kq2 / 2.20
kq6     = kq2 / 2.80
kq7     = kq2 / 3.50
; --- THE SPLIT, and it is IRREGULAR up the bank, which is what Table I actually shows.
;     Bowl 1's seven measured pairs, as (f_B - f_A)/f_AB: 0.454, 0.131, 0.334, 0.017,
;     0.375, 0.038, 0.299 %. A single fraction for all of them was the first version and
;     it was wrong twice over -- unfaithful to the table, and audible: twelve long-ringing
;     partials whose beats share one period all come back into phase together, and the
;     peak of the note then sat 11.6 dB above the strike at the long end of `ring`, which
;     this project's own axis probe reads as a fader. The measured pattern has no common
;     period, so they never re-align. `warble` scales the whole pattern; the shape is the
;     bowl's.
kwsc    = 0.30 + 4.26 * kwarb                      ; Bowl 1 at 0.3x .. Bowl 3's 2.07 % on the fundamental
kw2     = 0.00454 * kwsc
kw3     = 0.00131 * kwsc
kw4     = 0.00334 * kwsc
kw5     = 0.00017 * kwsc
kw6     = 0.00375 * kwsc
kw7     = 0.00038 * kwsc
; --- THE EXCITER. Struck is a short burst into a shell that then rings on its own; rubbed
;     is continuous, and Terwagne & Bush record what continuous friction does: the lowest
;     mode locks in and brings its own HARMONICS with it. So `sung` crossfades the drive
;     from a strike into a hold AND fades in a harmonic layer locked to the fundamental.
; --- THE MALLET, and its amplitude does NOT depend on Q. Measured on one `mode` over a
;     75x span of Q, a fixed impulse gives an attack level of -69.5 to -68.3 dB -- 1.2 dB
;     across the whole range -- while what changes is the DECAY: -102.0 dB over 5.7 s at
;     Q 330 against -1.4 at Q 25000. That is what Q means and it is what the mallet does,
;     so `ring` is a decay axis with a constant strike and needs no normalisation. An
;     earlier version divided the impulse by Q on the theory that a resonator's gain goes
;     with Q; that is true of its STEADY state, not of its response to a strike, and it
;     made the axis a 15 dB volume control.
;     NO NOISE EXCITER, deliberately, and this one is also measured rather than reasoned:
;     at Q 10000 a mode's bandwidth is 0.02 Hz, so noise through it is one sinusoid whose
;     amplitude random-walks over tens of seconds -- the same body measured -24.3 dB at
;     three seconds and -33.3 at 5.7. `struck_bar` and `cymbal` can hold a noise exciter
;     because their Q is 900-1400; at a bowl's Q it is not a drive, it is a lottery.
;     THE MALLET IS COMPUTED AT A-RATE, AND BOTH OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVES ARE WRONG HERE.
;     `expon` starts when the INSTRUMENT starts, so under a preroll -- and under any host
;     that keeps a voice alive between notes -- the strike has already decayed before the
;     note begins: the axis probe read the peak 13.0 dB apart across `ring` where the
;     body's own sample peak moves 0.89 dB. Hanging it on `knote` instead cures that and
;     brings a worse fault, because 1.8 ms is SHORTER THAN ONE CONTROL PERIOD -- so how
;     much of the pulse exists depends on the control rate, and the control rate follows
;     the sample rate. Measured on the two rates that matter: 44100, where a body gets
;     auditioned, against 176400, which is what the plugin actually compiles Csound at
;     (`lroOsFactor_ { 4 }` in PluginProcessor.h, capped at 200 kHz). The same body peaked
;     2.049 and 12.48 -- a factor of 6.09 -- and its centroid fell 377 to 259 Hz. The bank
;     is not at fault: `mpulse` alone measures 1.07x across those rates, and `interp` in
;     place of `a()` changed nothing, so it is not the staircase either.
;     So the weight is the SAME one-pole force step, taken where a sub-millisecond force
;     belongs: at audio rate, as a `tone` on the contact, at the corner the exponential
;     already named. Across those two rates it now measures 1.04x with the centroid 362
;     against 361 Hz. It also costs two thirds of the register tilt (12.61 dB from 110 to
;     880 Hz, now 4.20) and brings the keyboard inside the host's clip ceiling -- 23.32 at
;     110 Hz before, 2.80 after -- because how much of a 1.8 ms pulse survived one control
;     period was a function of pitch as much as of rate.
;     AND IT IS DETERMINISTIC. A mallet is a short force pulse, not noise: an exponential
;     force step is broadband on its own (one-pole, corner 1/(2*pi*0.0018) = 88 Hz, so
;     every mode gets excited and the higher ones a little less, which is what a soft
;     mallet does). Multiplying it by `rand` made the note's PEAK a random draw, and the
;     axis probe then read `bowl` and `warble` as faders at 1.0 and 3.5 dB when neither
;     touches the level -- it was measuring noise peaks.
;     TWO PARTS, because one alone does not do it. The exponential force step is the
;     mallet's WEIGHT and rolls off at 88 Hz, so on its own it leaves the upper modes
;     nearly unexcited -- measured, the body's colour then travelled 1 Hz over the note
;     and `project_lco_movement_by_default` is a platform requirement, not a preference.
;     A single-sample `mpulse` is the CONTACT and is flat to Nyquist. Together they are a
;     soft mallet on a bowl: everything rings, the top rings less, and the top dies first,
;     which is the colour travelling 360 Hz over the note.
;     AND IT IS RE-STRUCK AT EVERY NOTE, which needs the `reinit` below and not a
;     comment. `mpulse kamp, 0` emits ONE impulse at the instance's first sample, and the
;     host scores a single always-on instance (`i 1 0 2000000000`), so without this the bowl
;     is struck once when the orchestra is BUILT and every note after it only un-gates
;     the decaying residue. Measured before this line, at 220 Hz with the defaults: a
;     note begun at 0 s of instance uptime peaked 1.6132, at 2 s 0.8837, at 8 s 0.3634,
;     at 30 s 0.0193 -- 38 dB of difference made by nothing but how long the plugin had
;     been open. `plucked_wire` carries the same construction and the same warning for
;     the same reason. `BOWLSTRIKE` is a LABEL: a second copy of this body in one
;     instrument needs a different one.
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit BOWLSTRIKE
        endif
BOWLSTRIKE:
acon    mpulse 3.0, 0                               ; the contact, flat to Nyquist
        rireturn
aw      tone acon, 88.4                             ; the weight, 1/(2*pi*0.0018) = 88.4 Hz
aex     = acon + aw                                 ; a soft mallet on a bowl
; --- the bank. Each mode twice, split by kw, so the pair beats the way the table says.
ka2a    limit kc * kr2 * (1 - kw2/2), 20, 18000
ka2b    limit kc * kr2 * (1 + kw2/2), 20, 18000
ka3a    limit kc * kr3 * (1 - kw3/2), 20, 18000
ka3b    limit kc * kr3 * (1 + kw3/2), 20, 18000
ka4a    limit kc * kr4 * (1 - kw4/2), 20, 18000
ka4b    limit kc * kr4 * (1 + kw4/2), 20, 18000
ka5a    limit kc * kr5 * (1 - kw5/2), 20, 18000
ka5b    limit kc * kr5 * (1 + kw5/2), 20, 18000
ka6a    limit kc * kr6 * (1 - kw6/2), 20, 18000
ka6b    limit kc * kr6 * (1 + kw6/2), 20, 18000
ka7a    limit kc * kr7 * (1 - kw7/2), 20, 18000
ka7b    limit kc * kr7 * (1 + kw7/2), 20, 18000
kg3     = (kc * kr3 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg4     = (kc * kr4 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg5     = (kc * kr5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg6     = (kc * kr6 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg7     = (kc * kr7 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
a2a     mode aex, ka2a, kq2
a2b     mode aex, ka2b, kq2
a3a     mode aex, ka3a, kq3
a3b     mode aex, ka3b, kq3
a4a     mode aex, ka4a, kq4
a4b     mode aex, ka4b, kq4
a5a     mode aex, ka5a, kq5
a5b     mode aex, ka5b, kq5
a6a     mode aex, ka6a, kq6
a6b     mode aex, ka6b, kq6
a7a     mode aex, ka7a, kq7
a7b     mode aex, ka7b, kq7
; --- the (2,0) mode dominates: "mainly dominated by the first (2,0) shell mode"
ashell  = (a2a + a2b) * 1.000 \
        + (a3a + a3b) * 0.500 * kg3 \
        + (a4a + a4b) * 0.280 * kg4 \
        + (a5a + a5b) * 0.160 * kg5 \
        + (a6a + a6b) * 0.090 * kg6 \
        + (a7a + a7b) * 0.050 * kg7
; --- MODE LOCK-IN, and it is a SEPARATE LAYER because it is a separate spectrum. Rubbed
;     rather than struck, "the lowest mode is excited along with its harmonics, an effect
;     known as a mode 'lock in'" (Terwagne & Bush). Those are true harmonics of the (2,0)
;     mode and not shell modes, so re-tuning the bank would be the wrong move. It is
;     deterministic and not noise-driven, which is what friction locking onto a mode IS,
;     and it also keeps this half of the axis off the random walk above.
;     The pair beats here too: the rub excites both halves of the fundamental.
alk     poscil 0.50, kc * (1 - kw2/2), giSine
alkb    poscil 0.50, kc * (1 + kw2/2), giSine
kh2     = (kc * 2 < 16000 ? 0.30 : 0)               ; the same Nyquist gate the shell
kh3     = (kc * 3 < 16000 ? 0.12 : 0)               ;   bank carries -- without it the
kh4     = (kc * 4 < 16000 ? 0.05 : 0)               ;   harmonics fold at 1x oversampling
alk2    poscil kh2, kc * 2, giSine
alk3    poscil kh3, kc * 3, giSine
alk4    poscil kh4, kc * 4, giSine
