kbld    limit kbldr, 0, 1                            ; sqrt of a negative NaNs the whole voice
; --- levelled against the strike THROUGH THE NOTE, not at its peak, and the difference
;     matters: the rub STANDS while the strike decays, so the two can be matched at one
;     or the other and not at both. Over a four-second note at 220 Hz they now measure
;     -15.10 and -15.77 dB rms, 0.7 dB apart. What is left at the PEAK is 6.7 dB, and
;     that is a strike against no strike -- it is what the axis MEANS, not a fader. An
;     earlier 0.227 was levelled against a strike that was itself wrong (see the reinit
;     above) and left this axis moving 14.06 dB. This is a level match between two layers
;     of this body, not a curve over anyone's model.
alock   = (alk + alkb + alk2 + alk3 + alk4) * 0.60
; --- ONE equal-power crossfade, so `sung` moves the spectrum and not the level. Added
;     rather than crossfaded, it measured 22.3 dB across its own travel.
asig    = ashell * 0.42 * sqrt(1 - kbld) + alock * sqrt(kbld)
; --- ONE output scale, and it is headroom rather than taste. The loudest thing this body
;     can be asked for is a LOW bowl left to ring with the pair barely split -- 110 Hz,
;     `ring` 1.0, `warble` 0.0 -- because `mode`'s gain at resonance goes with Q over
;     frequency and nothing beats the peak down. Measured there at the rate the plugin
;     runs Csound, and with the instance old enough that nothing of the build-time strike
;     is left: 0.50 puts that corner at 2.20, under the host's transparent ceiling of
;     2.52, and the defaults at 0.76 at 220 Hz. That is quieter than the library's other
;     mode banks at their own defaults (`struck_bar` 1.96, `cymbal` 2.26) and it is the
;     price of a body whose corner space is this wide: a scale that put the defaults
;     among them would clip the bass. It moves no balance inside the body.
asig    = asig * kvol1 * 0.50
instruments.name: singing bowl

bowl.note: which measured bowl the mode series is. Not a curve and not a stretch factor: the two ends are Inácio et al. Table I/II, Bowl 2 (563 g, 152 mm, the flattest of their four) and Bowl 4 (the widest), so every position between them is between two real instruments. Bowl 2 runs 1, 2.7, 4.8, 7.5, 10.6, 14.2; Bowl 4 runs 1, 2.9, 5.7, 9.1, 13.1, 17.7, which sits almost exactly on the in-plane ring solution f_j ~ j(j^2-1)/sqrt(j^2+1) that Terwagne & Bush validate for j = 2..6. What it moves is where the partials SIT, not how bright the body is: from 0.0 to 1.0 at 220 Hz the (3,0) pair travels 593.5 to 637.5 Hz -- 124 cents -- and the (4,0) 1054 to 1259 Hz, while the spectral centroid stays within 1 Hz. So it retunes the inharmonicity and leaves the colour alone. It is not a level control either: 0.30 dB across its own travel.

small.gloss: Bowl 2 as measured: the flattest series, the partials closest in

wide.gloss: Bowl 4 as measured, and the ring solution: the partials furthest out

warble.note: how far the two halves of each mode pair stand apart -- the bowl's beating, and a measurement rather than a detune. Every mode in Inácio et al. Table I is a PAIR (f_nA, f_nB) because a real bowl is not perfectly axisymmetric; their model ‚introduc[es] a difference (or split) between the frequencies of each mode pair‘, and Terwagne & Bush confirm it independently: ‚Due to the bowl asymmetry, two peaks separated by several Hz arise and a beating mode is heard.‘ The pattern up the bank is IRREGULAR and that is the point -- Bowl 1's seven pairs measure 0.454, 0.131, 0.334, 0.017, 0.375, 0.038, 0.299 %, which have no common period, so twelve long-ringing partials never come back into phase together. One shared fraction was the first version and it was audible as a pulse. This axis scales the whole measured pattern; the shape is the bowl's. At 0.0 the split is 0.3x Bowl 1 (a 3.3 s beat at 220 Hz), at 0.164 Bowl 1 exactly, at 1.0 Bowl 3's measured 2.07 %. DECLARED AS THE LOUDNESS AXIS (`; LOUDNESS: warble`): because the body is read at the note's peak and the peak of a beat depends on where the halves are in their cycle, it moves the peak 3.56 dB on its own at 220 Hz. That is the beating, not a fader. For comparison, on the same measurement `bowl` moves 0.30 dB and `ring` 1.16 -- the strike really is the same at every Q, which is what its own note claims.

slow.gloss: the pair barely apart: one beat every three seconds at 220 Hz

measured.gloss: Bowl 1 exactly as the table has it: about one beat per second at 220 Hz

wide.gloss: Bowl 3's 2.07 %, the widest pair the paper measured: a fast shimmer

ring.note: how long the shell holds, and the range is the paper's: ‚dissipation is very low, with modal damping ratios typically in the range 0.002~0.015 % (higher values pertaining to higher-order modes). However, note that these values may increase one order of magnitude, or more, depending on how the bowls are actually supported or handled.‘ Q = 1/(2*zeta), so 25000 for a bowl standing free down to a few hundred for one held in a hand. The upper modes are damped harder than the fundamental (factors 1.3 to 3.5 up the bank), which is the paper's own direction and is why the note darkens as it rings. THE STRIKE DOES NOT CHANGE WITH IT, and that is measured rather than assumed: over a 75x span of Q a fixed impulse into one `mode` gives an attack of -69.5 to -68.3 dB while the DECAY goes from -102.0 dB over 5.7 s to -1.4. An earlier version divided the exciter by Q on the theory that a resonator's gain goes with Q -- true of its steady state, not of its response to a strike -- and that made this a 15 dB volume control. It does NOT change the level: 2.80 at 110 Hz and 2.24 at 220 against a clip ceiling of 2.75, both at `ring` 1.0, because the strike is the same at every Q.

held.gloss: the bowl in a hand, the paper's damped case: Q ~500, gone in about five seconds

mid.gloss: Q ~5200: a 7.6 s 1/e time, so it stands and darkens through any note

free.gloss: the lowest damping measured, Q 25000: it outlasts the longest note by far

sung.note: struck or rubbed, and they are two different spectra from one body. Terwagne & Bush: ‚When the bowl is rubbed with a leather wrapped mallet, the lowest mode is excited along with its harmonics, an effect known as a mode lock in.‘ So struck (0.0) gives the inharmonic shell modes above, and rubbed (1.0) gives the (2,0) mode plus TRUE HARMONICS of it -- which is why the lock-in is its own layer and not a retuning of the bank. The pair beats on that layer too, because the rub excites both halves of the fundamental. It crossfades equal-power over 0.35 s, because friction takes hold rather than jumping; added instead of crossfaded it measured 22.3 dB across its own travel. The two halves are levelled THROUGH the note, not at its peak: over four seconds at 220 Hz they measure -15.10 and -15.77 dB rms, 0.7 dB apart. What remains at the PEAK is 6.7 dB, and it is structural -- the struck body decays from its strike and the rubbed one has no strike at all, so the two cannot match at the peak AND through the note. This levelling favours where the note actually lives.

struck.gloss: the mallet: shell modes, mildly inharmonic, ringing down

half.gloss: the rub taking hold over the strike

rubbed.gloss: the mode lock-in: fundamental plus true harmonics, standing

instruments.why: clarinet / chalumeau / bass clarinet -- a cylindrical single-reed bore, on the physical model this build ships for exactly that: Csound's `wgclar`, Perry Cook's clarinet in Smith's digital-waveguide formulation (Cook, ICMC 1992; Smith, 'Physical Modeling using Digital Waveguides', CMJ 16(4), 1992). The odd-only series is not an approximation here, it is what a cylinder closed at the reed produces. Replaces an `foscili` pair at modulator ratio 2 that stood in for it: that had 0.00% of its energy above 2 kHz and no even partials at all (-140 dB), a clean odd stack with no air in it whatever, and it carried no knob the player could reach.
instruments.code:
; LOUDNESS: blow
; `blow` is the blowing PRESSURE on this reed and pressure carries level with it --
; a clarinet blown harder is louder, which is the physics and not an invented
; envelope. Every number here is measured at 176400, the rate the plugin compiles
; Csound at, and read after decimation to 44100; a bare-44100 reading of this model
; is a different instrument (same body, centroid 340 Hz there against 1235 Hz here).
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes -- 0 to -11 cents from 55 Hz to 880 Hz, rms flat within 0.21 dB
; across that span, so the chalumeau and the bass register are this same body played
; low. STANDS: it is driven and holds as long as the note does.
; `kngain` IS NOT BREATH NOISE, whatever its name and the manual suggest. BJ heard it
; first and the split confirms it: over this axis the INHARMONIC share moves 0.15% ->
; 0.31% while the HARMONIC energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. What it does is
; feed the reed nonlinearity, which redistributes the odd series upward -- at the low
; end the partials fall away smoothly (3rd..15th: -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5
; -24.1 dB), at the high end the upper ones carry the tone (-6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5
; -29.2 -4.9 -12.6). Real noise appears only past `kngain` 0.6, and there the rms has
; collapsed to 0.061 because the model has left self-oscillation. So there is no
; breath in this bore to reach for; a breath layer would have to be MIXED IN, which
; this instrument is entitled to do (BJ 2026-08-05: "das ist ein synth, also kann man
; rauschen zumischen lassen, auch im rezept") and which v1.0 does not yet do.
; THE TWO AXES ARE COUPLED IN THE MODEL and the ranges are picked so each still
; travels on its own. Below `kngain` 0.20 nothing at all comes up, and the pressure
; at which the reed opens falls as `kngain` rises: kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at
; 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.
; THE MOVEMENT IS THE BREATH, not a wobble laid on the pitch: a slow unsteadiness in
; the blowing pressure, which is what a player's breath does. It is small (0.02 of
; the pressure) and it stays inside the turbulent regime at every position of both
; knobs, because crossing that boundary inside a note is what an earlier, wider
; version did and it cost 58 dB of loudness travel in one note.
; NO ATTACK IS WRITTEN HERE and none can be. `wgclar`'s own `iatt` is dead in this
; host: one instance per voice is started at engine build and never restarted, so a
; note only unmutes a bore that is already standing -- measured with a preroll, 0.99
; of full level 5 ms after the gate opens, and IDENTICAL for a pressure ramp of
; 0.02 s and one of 0.24 s. A ramp changes only where the bore settles afterwards
; (hysteresis), which is a side effect and not an onset. The player's envelope owns
; the attack.
kovertone = 0.55   ; overtone [0.00..1.00]: how far up the reed is worked -- from a hollow chalumeau on its lowest partials to a bright reedy tone standing on its upper ones
kblow   = 0.55   ; blow [0.00..1.00]: how hard the reed is blown -- the pressure on the bore, soft and pure to driven and turbulent
kng     = 0.30 + 0.20 * kovertone                ; 0.50 is the ceiling: past it the model leaves
                                             ; self-oscillation entirely (rms 0.062 at 0.7).
                                             ; 0.30 is the dry end -- below 0.20 no pressure
                                             ; whatever brings breath out of the bore.
kwander oscili 0.02, 0.23, giSine            ; a player's breath is never quite steady
kpr     = 0.55 + 0.35 * kblow + kwander               ; started below the turbulent boundary a note stays
                                             ; dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured:
                                             ; floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 ->
                                             ; 18.0% at the same target), so the range begins above it.
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, kng, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff`, INERT in this build (output
                                             ; bit-identical -0.9 to 0.0 at both rates), so it sits at
                                             ; the documented value and never moves. kvamp is 0: no
                                             ; built-in vibrato. ONE wgclar and no more -- a second
                                             ; instance changes this one, 3rd partial -5.9 -> -14.1 dB.
asig    = asig * 1.30 * kvol1
instruments.name: clarinet

overtone.note: how far up the reed is worked -- `kngain` over 0.30..0.50. NOT breath noise, whatever the argument's name suggests: measured at 176400 and read after decimation to 44100, the inharmonic share moves only 0.15% -> 0.31% across this axis while the harmonic energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. It feeds the reed nonlinearity and the odd series redistributes upward -- 3rd to 15th partial -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5 -24.1 dB at the low end against -6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5 -29.2 -4.9 -12.6 at the high one, so it is a change of which partials carry the tone and not a tilt. 0.50 is a hard ceiling: real noise only appears past 0.6 and by then the model has left self-oscillation (rms 0.061 at 0.7). COUPLED TO `blow`: the pressure at which the reed opens falls as this rises -- kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.

hollow.gloss: the chalumeau, standing on its lowest partials

open.gloss: the upper odd partials coming up under the tone

reedy.gloss: bright, the tone carried by its upper partials

blow.note: how hard the reed is blown -- `kamp` over 0.50..0.90, which on this model is the blowing PRESSURE and not an output level. Measured at 176400 and read after decimation to 44100, at the authored `air`: the rms rises 0.21 -> 0.47 (7.2 dB) while the energy above 2 kHz goes 2.9% -> 35.3% and the centroid 446 -> 2046 Hz, so colour travels with the level rather than instead of it -- declared `; LOUDNESS: blow`, because a clarinet blown harder IS louder. Do not read the older 44100 figures for this argument: at a bare 44100 it shows a threshold at 0.76 that does not exist at the rate the plugin runs. The range stops at 0.90 because the model keeps rising past it with nothing new in the tone, and starts at 0.50 because a note begun below the turbulent boundary stays dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured: floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 -> 18.0%, same target pressure).

soft.gloss: pure and contained, the reed barely worked

spoken.gloss: the normal weight of the tone

driven.gloss: pushed until the reed turns turbulent

instruments.why: flute / recorder / piccolo / whistle / pan flute -- a blown air column: a hollow four-harmonic stack whose rolloff breathes on a three-second pressure cycle, with an octave layer beating against its own second harmonic; the blown character, not a physical bore model
instruments.code:
kbr0    poscil 0.5, 0.31             ; breath-pressure cycle, ~3 s
kfm0    = 0.24 + 0.16 * kbr0      ; pressure opens the harmonics
abd0    gbuzz 0.34, (kfreq * koct1), 4, 1, kfm0, giCos ; blown harmonic stack
kwo0    poscil 0.0009, 0.077         ; air-column wander, own rate
aoc0    poscil 0.05, (kfreq * koct1) * 2 * (1 + kwo0)  ; octave, beats with the body's 2nd
asig    = abd0 + aoc0
instruments.name: flute

instruments.why: brass -- trumpet / french horn / trombone / tuba / brass section: a twelve-harmonic stack whose rolloff opens once from dark to bright over the attack and then holds, voiced through a fixed 1200 Hz bell formant
instruments.code:
kop0    = 1 - exp(-knote * 2.2)       ; attack opens the series ONCE
kbm0    = 0.30 + kop0 * 0.42       ; dark at onset -> bright, then holds
klw0    poscil 0.0006, 0.083         ; lip instability, own rate
abz0    gbuzz 0.5, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + klw0), 12, 1, kbm0, giCos ; lip + bore
abl0    reson abz0, 1200, 900, 1   ; bell formant, FIXED in Hz
asig    = abz0 * 0.95 + abl0 * 0.40
instruments.name: brass

instruments.why: bowed string SECTION -- orchestral strings, a string ensemble, massed players (a single bowed instrument is `string`): three players sounding together, each with its own slow intonation drift and its own bow-pressure cycle, detuned against each other; a bright saw-family spectrum with a gentle harmonic-count breathing
instruments.code:
krm0    = min(sr * 0.47, 20000) / (kfreq * koct1)        ; harmonics that fit
kctr0   limit krm0 * 0.62, 1.6, 7 ; corner centre, capped
ksd0x0  poscil 0.0009, 0.061         ; player 1 intonation
ksb0x0  poscil 0.35, 0.089           ; player 1 bow pressure
asr0x0  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0000 * (1 + ksd0x0), 0
kbc0x0  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x0), 50, min(sr * 0.47, 20000) ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x0  tone asr0x0, kbc0x0
ksd0x1  poscil 0.0009, 0.073         ; player 2 intonation
ksb0x1  poscil 0.35, 0.107           ; player 2 bow pressure
asr0x1  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.0042 * (1 + ksd0x1), 0
kbc0x1  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x1), 50, min(sr * 0.47, 20000) ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x1  tone asr0x1, kbc0x1
ksd0x2  poscil 0.0009, 0.047         ; player 3 intonation
ksb0x2  poscil 0.35, 0.127           ; player 3 bow pressure
asr0x2  vco2 0.30, (kfreq * koct1) * 0.9958 * (1 + ksd0x2), 0
kbc0x2  limit (kfreq * koct1) * kctr0 * (1 + 0.7 * ksb0x2), 50, min(sr * 0.47, 20000) ; bow sharpens the corner
ase0x2  tone asr0x2, kbc0x2
aens0   = ase0x0 + ase0x1 + ase0x2 ; the desk

instruments.why: plucked string / guitar / harp / koto / pizzicato (a violin or cello PLUCKED): ONE real string, set going and then left to ring -- NOT the ensemble string machine (that is `strings`, detuned saws) and NOT the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (that is `harpsichord`, gbuzz choirs). The string is a comb resonator tuned to the played pitch. It has to be fed the whole time so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking -- but the feed arrives as scattered, time-smeared touches and the ring is kept long, so what is heard is the string and not what is driving it. A continuous wall of noise into the same resonator is audibly an electric string driver: aggressive and restless. Its top dies away after the attack the way a real string loses its brilliance -- twice over, fast for the first instant and slowly for the whole ring. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCK THAT IS ALLOWED TO DIE -- struck once and left to ring down under the key -- this entry cannot do it, because it is fed the whole time on purpose; `plucked_wire` is the one, a real Karplus-Strong wire with nothing driving it after the pluck. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. bow = plucked with a pick to drawn with a bow, pick = where the string is set going, from right at the bridge to at the middle, damp = left ringing to stopped under the hand A STRING DRAWN WITH A BOW -- violin, viola, cello, bass, arco -- is `bowed_string`: a real bow on a waveguide string. This entry's `bow` axis only thickens the dust that drives the resonator, and BJ never took it.

Bei bow nur sehr schwach", "sound ist insgesamt aber behaltenswert", "das gilt allerding seher für die tiefen Lagen bei C4 beginnt das rumbeln und klingeln" -- 2026-08-02: "'Damp' immer noch völlig unbrauchbar. Es muss entweder richtig verstanden werden oder auf 0 gesetzt und aus der liste genommen werden" -- 2026-08-02, nach Damp als Filtergrenzfrequenz und nach dem Klingeln: "ok, das ist noch nicht perfekt, wird aber akzeptiert als verifiziert - noch beta" -- "ok, dann abgenommen"“ — gehört über tools/lco_ab_string_damp/ -- die Damp-Achse in fünf Stufen bei A2 und A4, daneben dieselben zehn Stufen aus der Verdrahtung, die er verworfen hatte (aus 08defb07 gelesen, nicht nachgetippt), alle zwanzig Dateien unter EINEM gemeinsamen Pegel. Davor tools/lco_ab_string_bowed/ für den gestrichenen Klang.

bow.note: how the string is set going, and that is the whole difference between a guitar and a cello. A pick or a fingernail lets go in an instant, so everything in the string is woken at once and the sound arrives bright and then falls away. A bow never lets go: the hair grabs and slips and grabs again, feeding the string the whole time, so the top is rubbed off but nothing dies -- the tone stands and breathes instead. In the code this is how DENSELY the drive arrives: separate touches at the plucked end, a steady draw at the bowed one. Measured across the axis the colour travels from 4812 Hz down to 3463 Hz while how sharply the string rings does not change (34.3 -> 33.6 dB) and the loudness moves 0.04 dB.

plucked.gloss: picked and let go: bright at the front, then darkening

bowed.gloss: drawn with a bow: standing, breathing, the top rubbed off

pick.note: where along the string it is set going, as a fraction of its length. Not a tone control -- geometry: the body subtracts a copy of the drive delayed by `pick` of a period, so the harmonic whose node falls on that spot cannot be given any energy and is simply missing. That harmonic is 1/pick, so the axis is a NOTCH WALKING DOWN through the harmonics as it rises, and it bites hardest where 1/pick lands on one. Measured at 220 Hz, how far that harmonic sits below its neighbours: 0.10 takes 39 dB out of the 10th, 0.125 36 dB out of the 8th, 0.167 34 dB out of the 6th, 0.20 41 dB out of the 5th, 0.25 46 dB out of the 4th, 0.333 42 dB out of the 3rd, and 0.50 cancels EVERY even harmonic at once (44 dB, odd-to-even 44.1 dB) -- the hollow, woody one. BETWEEN those positions the notch falls between two harmonics and does much less: at the shipped default 0.185 the null sits at 5.4, BETWEEN two harmonics, so no harmonic is cancelled at all -- the fifth reads 1.8 to 10.0 dB below its neighbours depending on register (the comb's closed form 2|sin(pi n beta)| gives 6.6 dB; the spread is the broadband drive scattering the partial readings, not the axis), against the 34 to 46 dB above where the null lands ON one. That is why that one setting sounds like no setting at all. The default is 0.185 because that is what the entry has always played; if the sound wants its pluck position HEARD, start it at 0.25, 0.333 or 0.50. Loudness across the whole axis and four registers: 0.035 dB.

wiry.gloss: close to the bridge: the tenth harmonic cancelled, thin and hard

hollow.gloss: a quarter along: the fourth harmonic gone, 46 dB down

middle.gloss: over the middle: EVERY even harmonic gone at once, hollow and woody -- a clarinet made of string

damp.note: how freely the string is allowed to ring, as with the flat of the hand laid on it. Damping a string is a FREQUENCY-DEPENDENT loss and nothing else: the hand takes the highs first and the low partials keep going, which is why a muted string reads as dull rather than as quiet. In a digital string that loss is the loop filter (Jaffe & Smith, CMJ 7(2) 1983). `streson` exposes no loop filter, so THIS AXIS IS NOT ONE: it is the cutoff of the `tone` standing in FRONT of the resonator, scaled by `1 - 0.85 * kdamp`, and the difference is measurable and must be known before choosing a setting. A loop filter applies its loss once per round trip, so the loss compounds; a one-pole on the drive applies it once, and once its cutoff is below the played fundamental the RATIO between partial n and partial 1 stops changing. The axis therefore SATURATES, and how much of it is left depends on the register. Centroid travel over the whole axis, measured at the 4x the LRO runs: 1.55 octaves at 55 Hz, 1.58 at 110, 1.38 at 220, 1.05 at 440, 0.48 at 880 and 0.26 at 1760 (at 44100 it is 1.29 / 1.20 / 0.91 / 0.65 / 0.41 / 0.21). USE IT BELOW ABOUT 440 Hz. Above C5 it is worth less than this entry's own `bow`, which BJ heard as barely audible at 0.77 octaves. It is also back-loaded: at 220 Hz the four quarters give 0.18 / 0.25 / 0.36 / 0.59 octaves, so the last quarter is over 40 % of the whole travel and the `damped` anchor at 0.5 sits at less than a third of it. SECOND EFFECT, declare it rather than discover it: the scaling multiplies the whole `kcut` product, note envelopes included, so damping also softens this body's attack colour instead of sharpening it the way a real loop filter would -- the ratio of the first 50 ms centroid to the sustained one falls from 3.73x to 2.19x at 880 Hz and 2.87x to 1.87x at 440. `streson`'s own feedback is NOT touched and must not be: it is one flat gain for every partial, so lowering it does not damp anything -- it removes the resonance and leaves the broadband drive, which the closing `balance` then amplifies. That is what this axis used to do, and it is worth writing down because a comb-contrast meter certified it: balance had to apply 3.7x at 0 and 15.8x at 1, and the centroid ROSE 3099 -> 4924 Hz. Brighter and noisier, i.e. the opposite. Loudness over the whole damp x pick grid at six registers and both rates: 0.09 dB; true peaks 0.65 to 1.05 against the host's 2.523. THE SHIPPED STRING IS THE OPEN ONE, so the default is 0 and the axis only ever damps.

open.gloss: left to ring: the full top of the string, a clear singing note

damped.gloss: a hand resting on it: the top rolled off, the note dulls but is still a note -- and this is under a third of the travel, not half of it

muted.gloss: palm-muted: dark and dull in the low and middle registers, the highs gone and the low partials still ringing. Above C5 the axis has little left to take

instruments.why: a string DRAWN WITH A BOW -- violin, viola, cello, double bass, anything arco: a real bow on a real string, not a resonator fed with noise. The head's `t5bow` is a waveguide string in velocity waves with the bow's friction curve at the contact point (Smith, ICMC 1986; McIntyre, Schumacher & Woodhouse, JASA 1983): the hair sticks to the string and slips off it once per period, and that stick-slip IS the tone -- it stands as long as the bow is drawn, it is periodic, and nothing in it is noise. The string loses its top at the bridge through a one-pole whose cutoff is in Hz, so it is the same instrument at 44100 and at the 4x the plugin runs (which `wgbow`, the only other bow in this Csound, is not: its loss filter is relative to the sample rate and at 4x it is 1.6-1.9 octaves too bright). What radiates goes through a BOX: the violin's four signature body modes and the bridge hill as `mode` filters, scaled by `box` down to a cello. A bow ARM moves weight and speed over the note -- the hair bites at the start and lets go, and keeps drifting afterwards -- all of it in the arm, none of it on the pitch. NOT `string`, whose `bow` axis only thickens the `dust` that drives a comb resonator (that entry is the PLUCKED string: guitar, harp, pizzicato), and NOT `strings`, the ensemble machine of detuned saws. Cost: about 1.9 % of one core per voice at 4x against 0.8 % for `string`; sixteen always-on voices are roughly a third of a core. place = where along the string the bow is drawn, gut = the string itself from dark gut to bright steel, box = the size of the body from cello to violin
instruments.code:
; A BOWED STRING -- a bow on a string, the arm that draws it, and the box it is mounted on.
;
; STRING  the head's `t5bow`: a waveguide string in velocity waves with the bow's friction
;         curve at the contact point (Smith, ICMC 1986; McIntyre, Schumacher & Woodhouse,
;         JASA 1983). The hair sticks to the string and slips off it, and that cycle IS the
;         tone: nothing in it is noise. The string loses its top at the bridge through a
;         one-pole whose cutoff is in Hz, so it is the same string at 44100 and at the 4x
;         the plugin runs -- which is what `wgbow` is not.
; ARM     the stroke. At the start of a note the hair bites -- more weight, less speed --
;         and lets go over the first tenth of a second; afterwards weight and speed keep
;         drifting, because a drawn bow never stands still. All of it in the arm, none of
;         it on the pitch. The weight itself is not a knob: measured over slope 1.0..2.5
;         it moves the colour by a tenth and nothing else a player would reach for, and
;         heavier than slope 1.25 (lower numbers are more weight) it lets the string fall
;         into double-period motion away from the bridge. It stands at 2.0, where the bow
;         holds the fundamental at every pitch.
; BOX     what radiates is the string at the bridge through the body: the violin's four
;         signature modes as `mode` filters -- A0 272 Hz, CBR 407, B1- 462, B1+ 551 -- and
;         the bridge hill around 2.3 kHz (J. Woodhouse, Euphonics 5.3). `box` scales them;
;         at 0.37 they sit where a cello's do. The Q values are not in the source and are
;         not pretended to be: they are this entry's, by ear. Without the box a waveguide
;         string is a buzz. Around 880-1100 Hz the hill lifts the second and third
;         partial above the fundamental, as a violin's body does at A5.
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes, to about kplace * 14700 Hz at 44100 and kplace * 19600 Hz at 4x
;         (1.9 and 2.5 kHz at the default place); above that the bow walks toward the
;         middle by itself, and above about 6 kHz the pitch is wrong. The bowed note sits a few
;         cents SHARP, growing with pitch and with darkness -- the hair catches the
;         smeared corner as soon as it enters the stick window, before it has fully
;         arrived. Measured at the defaults, both rates: +0.5 c at 55 Hz, +1 at 110, +2 at
;         220, +4 at 440, +8 at 880, +13 at 1320. The free string (bow removed) is on
;         kfreq to 0.01 cents at both rates; the rest is the bow's.
; DECAY   none: the bow is always drawn and the host's envelope owns the note.
kplace  = 0.130  ; place [0.10..0.20]: where along the string the bow is drawn, near the bridge to a fifth along
kgut    = 0.60   ; gut [0.00..1.00]: the string itself, from gut (dark and warm) to steel (bright and wiry)
kbox    = 1.00   ; box [0.35..1.20]: the size of the body, from a cello up past a violin
kf      limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
kcatch  = exp(-knote * 14.0)                             ; the hair bites, then lets go
kdraw   poscil 0.12, 0.190                               ; the weight the arm carries drifts
kdraw2  poscil 0.07, 0.310
kbreath poscil 0.15, 0.130                               ; and so does how fast it is drawn
kslope  limit 2.0 * (1 - 0.30 * kcatch + kdraw + kdraw2), 0.8, 2.5   ; the weight: STK's slope, 1 = leaning in
kspeed  = 0.10 * (1 - 0.60 * exp(-knote * 30.0)) * (1 + kbreath)
kcut    = 1400 * exp(1.7918 * kgut)                      ; 1400 Hz (gut) .. 8400 Hz (steel), 4100 at the default
kcut    limit kcut, min(3 * kf, 20000), 20000            ; a string cannot be darker than its own third partial
astr    t5bow kf, kspeed, kslope, kplace, kcut
aa0     mode astr, 272 * kbox, 18                        ; the air through the f-holes
acbr    mode astr, 407 * kbox, 20                        ; and the three wood modes
ab1m    mode astr, 462 * kbox, 25
ab1p    mode astr, 551 * kbox, 25
ahill   mode astr, 2300 * kbox, 4                        ; the bridge hill
abody   = aa0 * 0.050 + acbr * 0.035 + ab1m * 0.040 + ab1p * 0.040 + ahill * 0.25
abodyb  balance abody, astr, 1                           ; the box is a FILTER, not a fader:
amix    = astr * 0.30 + abodyb * 0.85                    ;   held against what went into it
aref    poscil 0.35, 400                                 ; a fixed-loudness yardstick, as `string`
abal    balance amix, aref                               ;   has it: place and gut move the
asig    = abal * 0.85                                    ;   colour, not the level
instruments.name: bowed string

place.note: where along the string the bow is drawn, as a fraction of its length from the bridge. Geometry, not a tone control: the bow splits the string into two delay lines and the harmonic whose node sits under the hair is starved, so the colour is a COMB walking through the partials, and what moves most is the character of the stick-slip, not the brightness. Measured at 220 Hz, 4x: centroid 2409 Hz at 0.10, 2308 at 0.13, 2465 at 0.16, 2582 at 0.20 (273 Hz of travel), comb contrast 59 -> 55 dB, loudness 0.01 dB. THE RANGE IS WHERE THE BOW HOLDS THE FUNDAMENTAL: at the fixed weight the string falls into double-period motion from about 0.22 outward (a sub-octave 10-17 dB under the note at 110-440 Hz, measured 0.24 and 0.25), and nearer the bridge than 0.10 the bow catches the octave or the twelfth above about 880 Hz, as a real bow does below Schelleng's minimum force. Inside 0.10..0.20 the sub-harmonic stays below -50 dB at every tested pitch 55-1760 Hz and both rates. The bridge-side line can be no shorter than two sub-blocks plus one sample, so above kplace * sr / (2 * iK + 1) -- about kplace * 14700 Hz at 44100 and kplace * 19600 Hz at 4x, 1.9 and 2.5 kHz at the default -- the bow walks toward the middle by itself, and above about 6 kHz the pitch is wrong.

ponticello.gloss: close to the bridge: glassy and thin, the hair biting hard

normale.gloss: the ordinary place, an eighth of the string: full and even

tasto.gloss: over the end of the fingerboard: softer, rounder, the top held back

gut.note: the string itself: how much of its top it loses at the bridge on every round trip. This IS a loop filter -- the one-pole at the bridge (Jaffe & Smith, CMJ 7(2) 1983) with its cutoff in Hz, 1400 Hz at 0 rising to 8400 Hz at 1 (4100 at the default), so it compounds once per period and the string darkens the way a real one does, and it is the same string at 44100 and at the plugin's 4x. Measured at 220 Hz, 4x: centroid 1748 Hz at 0, 1841 at 0.3, 2308 at 0.6, 3076 at 1 (1329 Hz of travel); at 880 Hz 4023 -> 5570 Hz; loudness 0.01 dB; comb contrast unchanged (58-59 dB). TWO THINGS TO KNOW. First, a string cannot be darker than its own third partial, or the bow has nothing left to grip: the cutoff is floored at 3 x the played pitch, so above about 440 Hz the dark end saturates (at 880 Hz, 0 and 0.3 read the same). Second, darkness pulls the pitch: the darker the string, the more the Helmholtz corner is smeared at the bridge and the earlier the hair catches it, so the note sits SHARP -- at 440 Hz +6 cents at 0, +3 at 0.3, +2 at 0.6, +1 at 1; at 880 Hz +14 at 0, +6 at 0.6, +3 at 1. Declared, not tuned out: it is the model's own behaviour and a fitted correction would be a number laid over it.

gut.gloss: a gut string: dark, warm, the top gone -- for the low and middle registers

wound.gloss: a wound string: the ordinary singing string, clear but not wiry

steel.gloss: bare steel: bright and wiry, every partial present

box.note: the size of the body the string is mounted on. The box is a bank of five `mode` filters at the violin's signature frequencies -- A0 272 Hz (the air through the f-holes), CBR 407, B1- 462, B1+ 551 and the bridge hill around 2300 Hz (J. Woodhouse, Euphonics 5.3) -- and `box` scales all five together: at 1.0 a violin, at 0.37 the modes land where a cello's do (A0 100 Hz, B1 171/204 Hz, hill 850 Hz), at 1.2 a small fiddle. The Q values (18/20/25/25/4) are not in the source and are this entry's, by ear. The bank is held against the string with `balance`, so the box is a filter and never a fader: loudness 0.01 dB over the range. Measured at 220 Hz, 4x: centroid 2978 Hz at 0.37 (the cello body sits BELOW a 220 Hz note and leaves it bright), 2252 at 0.7, 2308 at 1.0, 2164 at 1.2 (813 Hz of travel), comb contrast 52-59 dB. Around 880-1100 Hz the hill lifts the second and third partial 4-7 dB above the fundamental, as a violin's body does at A5; at 0.37 that region moves down to about 330-410 Hz.

cello.gloss: a cello's box: the air at 100 Hz, the wood at 170-200 Hz, the hill at 850

viola.gloss: a viola's box, between the two

violin.gloss: a violin's box: A0 272, B1 462/551, the hill at 2.3 kHz

instruments.why: a wire under tension, plucked once and then left alone: the note is made by the pluck and nothing feeds it afterwards, so it rings and dies the way a real wire does -- long and singing at the bottom of the keyboard, a short bright tick at the top. This is NOT `string`, which is a comb resonator fed the whole time so that a held note stands; it is the other thing, an actual travelling wave in a wire, and it is the only entry in the library that fades by itself. Karplus-Strong with the Jaffe-Smith extensions (David A. Jaffe and Julius O. Smith, 'Extensions of the Karplus-Strong Plucked-String Algorithm', Computer Music Journal 7(2), 1983), as Csound's `wgpluck2` implements it: two delay rails with a one-pole reflection filter standing in for the bridge. THREE THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE REACHING FOR IT. (1) IT TAKES THE KEY AT THE START OF THE NOTE AND THEN HOLDS IT. `wgpluck2` reads its frequency at i-rate, so the `reinit` on `ktrig` in the code is what makes it play the note at all -- and glide, pitch bend, vibrato and everything else on the pitch bus do not reach it once the note has begun. A legato slide leaves the wire at the pitch it was plucked at. A note that has to bend needs a pitch-following body beside it via `+`. (2) IT DECAYS, and how fast depends steeply on the pitch. Measured at the oscillator's default 4x oversampling, time to fall 20 dB: at refl 0.70 a note at 110 and 220 Hz has still not dropped 20 dB after 25 seconds, 440 Hz takes 4.4 s and 880 Hz 0.54 s; at refl 0.85 that is 8.5 s at 220, 1.05 s at 440 and 0.14 s at 880. So a long held note in the top octave will have gone silent by itself while the key is still down. That is the wire, not a fault -- but it is why this entry does not answer a prompt that asks for a sustained tone. The ring length also follows the LRO's oversampling setting, and steeply: at 1x that same 440 Hz note is down in 0.18 s where 4x gives 2.3 s. The model grows its delay line by whole periods until it holds at least 512 samples and rescales the reflection to match, so a shorter line -- a lower rate or a higher note -- ends up with a lossier bridge. It cannot be undone from outside: unwinding that rescaling would need a reflection below zero, which the model does not accept. Every figure here is at the default. (3) IT PLAYS SLIGHTLY FLAT, more so the higher the note and the higher refl. The bridge filter's pole is refl itself, so raising it adds delay to the loop, and the loop's length is the pitch; the delay line is also truncated to whole samples, which bites harder the shorter it is. Measured across the axis: within 4 cents at 110 and 220 Hz, within 18 at 440, and up to 44 cents flat at 880. The mechanism is read off the model's own source; the size of it is not derived, it is declared, and that is why the axis stops at 0.85. ABOVE THE AXIS IS COLOUR, NOT A NOTE. refl 0.90 to 0.98 is a different thing altogether: at 0.98 the sound is gone in 0.17 s at 220 Hz and sits 91 cents flat there, 172 cents at 440. What is left is a crackle, a small dry transient. Worth having -- layered under a pitched body with `+`, never asked to carry the pitch. THE PICKUP POINT IS THE SECOND AXIS. `pick` is where along the wire the sound is heard, and it is real geometry: a harmonic whose still point falls on that spot is simply missing. At 220 Hz, read over the first half-second because the note is already dying after that, the second harmonic runs from -7.0 dB below the fundamental at 0.25 to -11.0 at 0.35, and the third drops into a 68 dB hole at 0.33 -- wiry, then reedy, then round. It moves the LEVEL as well, and the body declares that instead of hiding it (`; LOUDNESS: pick`): across the axis the peak falls 1.25 dB while the note's settled energy RISES 1.75, in opposite directions, and the peak moves by the same amount at every register (-1.24 to -1.25 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz). What travels is the distance between them -- the peak sits 9.7 dB above the settled level at 0.25 and 6.7 dB at 0.35 -- because the wave is spiky near the end of the wire and smooth further along. That is a pluck being a transient, not a volume control, and it is the case §4 stopped judging by threshold on 2026-07-27. Both figures are `lco_measure`'s own peak and rms at the oscillator's default 4x. THE AXIS STOPS AT 0.35 FOR MOVEMENT, NOT FOR LOUDNESS. Raising the pickup damps the colour's travel over the note (46 Hz at 0.25, 20 at 0.35, 16 at 0.37), and at 0.37 combined with the shortest ring (refl 0.85) the body stands still outright when the LRO is run at 1x oversampling. 0.35 is the last point that still moves at every refl and every oversampling setting. Beyond it: at 0.50 the colour stands still at 55, 110 and 220 Hz, and past 0.50 nothing is new -- that is the middle of the wire and everything beyond mirrors what came before, 0.80 measuring within 3 dB of 0.20 over the first six partials. The middle itself, 0.50, kills the even harmonics outright (second harmonic 43 dB down at the attack) and stands still: a striking sound, and a deliberate one -- set it by hand, outside the axis. TWO NOTES ON THE CODE. There is deliberately NO `dcblock`: `wgpluck2` produces no DC worth blocking here (0.05 % of rms at worst), while `dcblock2`'s corner scales with the sample rate, so at the oscillator's 4x it becomes an ~800 Hz highpass that takes 23 dB out of a note at 110 Hz -- it destroys exactly the low end this body is good at. And `PLUCKWIRE:` is a LABEL, which cannot be indexed the way this library's variable names are: a second copy of this body in the same instrument must be given a different label. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCKED SOUND THAT STANDS while the key is held, this is the wrong entry and `string` is the right one -- same family, fed continuously, so a held note does not die. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. refl = how long it rings.

refl.note: how long the wire rings on after the pluck. Low is the long one: at 0.70 a note below about 300 Hz simply does not stop inside the note, and 440 Hz takes 4.4 s to fall 20 dB; at 0.85 that same 440 Hz is down in 1.05 s and 880 Hz in 0.14 s. So the axis runs from a wire left ringing to a short dry pluck, and it shortens much faster the higher you play. It also detunes: the note goes flat as the axis rises, measured +3.2 down to -3.9 cents at 220 Hz across the window and -4.0 to -18.2 at 440. That is what stops the axis at 0.85 rather than at 0.98, where the model still runs but the pitch is no longer the played one -- that region is a crackle, not a note, and the entry text says how to use it. The two loudness meters disagree on this axis and the difference IS the parameter: the attack does not move at all (peak spread 0.0 dB at 110, 220 and 440 Hz), while the note's total energy falls -- 0.5 dB at 110 Hz, 2.9 at 220, 6.1 at 440 -- because a shorter ring simply holds less of it. It is not a fader; it is the ring length being what it says.

ringing.gloss: left to ring: below 300 Hz it never stops inside the note

plucked.gloss: an ordinary pluck, ringing but clearly dying

dry.gloss: short and dry, and already a few cents flat

pick.note: where along the wire the sound is picked up, as a fraction of its length. A harmonic with a node at that point is cancelled, so the axis runs wiry (near the end, all harmonics present and the second only 7 dB down at the attack) through hollow (0.33, where the third harmonic falls into a 68 dB hole) to round. It is a TIMBRE axis that also moves the level, declared as such in the body: from 0.25 to 0.35 the peak falls 1.25 dB while the four-second energy rises 1.75, so neither meter alone is 'the loudness' -- what moves is the distance between them, 9.7 dB down to 6.7. The axis ends at 0.35 because the colour's travel over the note thins out as the pickup rises (46 Hz at 0.25, 20 at 0.35) and at 0.37 with the shortest ring the body stops moving altogether at 1x oversampling; past 0.50 the wire mirrors itself.

wiry.gloss: near the end of the wire: spiky, all harmonics, hard attack

hollow.gloss: the third harmonic cancelled -- reedy, a little nasal

round.gloss: smoother and softer-edged, the last point that still moves at every refl

instruments.why: supersaw / hypersaw -- the trance and rave lead, and the JP-8000's string pads. Seven sawtooth oscillators, one of them the played note and six standing off it. This is a DIGITAL oscillator and that is the whole reason it is its own entry: the saws are deliberately not band limited, so they alias, and Szabo names that fold-back as one of the four things every other emulation misses -- it is what makes the sound airy. Built from Adam Szabo, `How to Emulate the Super Saw`, BSc thesis, KTH Stockholm 2010 (TRITA-CSC-E 2010:131), which measured a Roland JP-8000 and JP-8080: the detune offsets (table 1), the 11th degree detune curve (fig 7), the two mix curves (fig 11), the pitch-tracking high pass on the first harmonic (fig 14/15) and the free-running random phases (fig 18-21). `detune` and `mix` are the machine's own two knobs.

detune.note: how far the six side saws stand off the centre one. The knob is not proportional: Szabo fitted an 11th degree polynomial through 17 measured settings, and it stays nearly flat to 0.5, steepens, then rises drastically after 0.9. So most of the travel is fine tuning -- measured on the outermost saw at 220 Hz: +0.6 cents at 0, +8.7 at 0.25, +18.1 at 0.5, +44.5 at 0.75, +176.7 at 1.0. The offsets are not symmetric and the centre saw is never detuned at all. The beating between the seven is the movement of this body: 2.3 dB at 0, 9.5 dB at 0.5.

tight.gloss: all seven on the note; one thick saw, barely moving

classic.gloss: +18 cents on the outer saw -- the pad and string spread

wide.gloss: +177 cents, close to a chord; the screaming lead end

mix.note: the six side saws against the centre one. Turning it up pulls the centre saw DOWN in a straight line while the six come up in a parabola; they meet at 0.75, not at the maximum the JP-8000 manual claims. Both curves are Szabo's fits to the measured amplitudes. Level follows: 3.8 dB from 0 to 0.75, because six saws add incoherently where one does not.

centred.gloss: the six are almost silent -- a single aliasing saw

even.gloss: all seven at the same level, where they were measured to meet

hollow.gloss: the centre pulled under the six; the note itself recedes

instruments.why: hard sync / oscillator sync -- the classic tearing sync lead: a slave saw restarted by the master every cycle, its ratio sweeping 1.5x..3.7x
instruments.code:
ivph0   = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; per-voice phase
kvdr0   poscil 0.0007, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph0
kswp0   oscili 1.1, 0.16            ; slave-ratio sweep
krat0   = 2.6 + kswp0            ; 1.5 .. 3.7 x master
azro0   = 0
amst0, asyn0  syncphasor (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kvdr0), azro0
aslv0, adum0  syncphasor (kfreq * koct1) * krat0, asyn0
asig    = (aslv0 * 2 - 1) * 0.45  ; hard-synced saw
instruments.name: sync

instruments.why: harpsichord / cembalo / spinet / virginal -- a plucked keyboard: two bright gbuzz choirs, an 8' and a 4' a hair sharp, drifting against each other; the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (a real plucked string is `string`)
instruments.code:
khw80   poscil 0.00040, 0.071        ; 8' choir tuning drift
khw40   poscil 0.00055, 0.094        ; 4' choir, incommensurate
ah80    gbuzz 0.56, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + khw80), 9, 1, 0.80, giCos ; 8' choir, bright
ah40    gbuzz 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0031 * (1 + khw40), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 4' choir
asig    = ah80 + ah40
instruments.name: harpsichord

instruments.why: chiptune -- the NES / Game Boy / C64 voice: the duty cycle STEPS between three fixed settings (12.5%, 25%, 50%) instead of gliding, giving the hard retro timbre switches
instruments.code:
kst0    oscili 1.49, 0.9            ; slow 3-zone selector
kdt0    = (kst0 > 0.5 ? 0.125 : (kst0 > -0.5 ? 0.25 : 0.5))
kdw0    tonek kdt0, 30          ; de-click the duty step
ach0    vco2 0.6, (kfreq * koct1), 2, kdw0     ; stepped chip duty
asig    = ach0 - 0.6 * (2 * kdw0 - 1) ; remove the duty's DC offset, A*(2d-1)
instruments.name: chiptune

instruments.why: theremin / ondes martenot / musical saw -- the breathing, near-vocal purity of a swept heterodyne tone: an almost pure tone whose odd harmonics waver slowly under a heterodyne nonlinearity
instruments.code:
kwv0    poscil 0.5, 0.9              ; slow timbre waver
kndx0   = 0.42 + 0.34 * kwv0       ; heterodyne mix depth
asig    foscili 0.55, (kfreq * koct1), 1, 2, kndx0, giSine ; heterodyne nonlinearity
instruments.name: theremin

instruments.why: analogue oscillator / vco / dco: ONE waveform generator with every control the shape needs. `wave` picks between two vco2 generators -- the ramp one and the pulse one -- and `width` is the SAME position on both: the fraction of the period spent in the first phase, symmetric at 0.5. So a waveform is a pair of numbers, not a name: a triangle is wave 0 with width 0.5, a saw wave 0 with width near either end, a square wave 1 with width 0.5, a narrow pulse wave 1 with width 0.12. The width is a modulation DESTINATION -- whatever writes it, an LFO, an envelope, a hand, is pulse width modulation, and the measure of that movement is the interval of widths it covers. `finetune` shifts the pitch in cents so several layers can be detuned against each other; `drive` is not a shaper at all: it is how hard this oscillator is driven INTO the synth's filter, 0 dB up to as loud as the body may be, so the saturating element is the ladder's own input stage -- a Minimoog fed through its External Input Volume, which is what the sound is named after; `age` is component drift, and it is the axis between the two kinds of machine in that list: at 0 nothing drifts and this is a DCO, a digitally clocked pitch, while the drift itself is what a VCO does. Level MOVES across `drive`, by design and by measurement -- that axis is a level; across `width` it moves too, and must -- see both parameters.
instruments.code:
; LOUDNESS: width
; LOUDNESS: wave
; the pulse generator's level follows its width: what is left once the DC A*(2w-1)
; is taken out is 2A*sqrt(w(1-w)) -- 3.77 dB down at 0.12 and 11.28 at 0.02. So
; `width` moves the level on that generator, and `wave`, which decides how much of
; it is heard, carries that with it. The ramp generator has no such term: rms
; 1/sqrt(3) at every width. A pulse gets quieter the narrower it gets, and that IS
; pulse width modulation (BJ 2026-07-28, LCO_CONCEPT.md section 4).
; LOUDNESS: drive
; `drive` is the LEVEL this oscillator sends into the synth's filter, and there is
; no shaper in here at all. That is what the knob is on a Minimoog: the External
; Input Volume feeds the mixer at high gain and the LADDER's own transistor stages
; do the saturating. Measured on BJ's Minimoog V recording of exactly that
; (2026-08-01): the level rises 16.00 dB from clean to driven, the crest falls
; 2.31 to 1.65 and the spectral centroid falls 3253 Hz to about 600 -- the driven
; sound is DARKER and denser, not brighter. A waveshaper held to the clean level
; cannot produce any of those three; a pregain into a saturating filter produces
; all three. So this axis moves the level, and must.

kwave   = 0.00    ; wave [0..1]: which generator -- 0 the ramp, 1 the pulse
kwidth  = 0.02    ; width [0.02..0.98]: the fraction of the period spent in the first phase
kfinetune = 0.00  ; finetune [-50..50]: cents off the played note
kdrive  = 0.00    ; drive [0..1]: how hard this oscillator is driven into the filter
kage    = 0.35    ; age [0..1]: component drift -- pitch, width and level wobble

ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)          ; each voice enters the drift elsewhere
kdrf    poscil 0.007 * kage, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph
kjit    poscil 0.012 * kage, 0.057             ; age: width jitter
klvl    oscili 0.030 * kage, 0.7               ; age: level wobble
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1) * (2 ^ (kfinetune / 1200)) * (1 + kdrf)

kfold   = kwidth + kjit                        ; ONE width, and both generators read it
kdw     limit abs(kfold - 2 * round(kfold * 0.5)), 0.01, 0.99
                                               ; the clamp sits OUTSIDE the axis on
                                               ;   purpose. At 0.02 it would sit on
                                               ;   the width's own end and eat the
                                               ;   negative half of `kjit` there --
                                               ;   the drift would stop at exactly
                                               ;   the setting the entry ships. 0.01
                                               ;   and 0.99 is what Csound asks for.
                                               ; it FOLDS at 0 and 1 rather than wrapping:
                                               ;   w and 1-w are the same spectrum, so the
                                               ;   sound travels the same path either way,
                                               ;   but a wrap makes vco2 jump across its
                                               ;   own table discontinuity and emit a lone
                                               ;   one-sample spike. Measured over 8 s at
                                               ;   full depth: 15 wrapping, 0 folding.
aramp   vco2 0.6, kf0, 4, kdw                  ; ramp: 0.5 a triangle, either end a saw
apuls   vco2 0.6, kf0, 2, kdw                  ; pulse: 0.5 a square, either end narrow
apuls   = apuls - 0.6 * (2 * kdw - 1)          ; a width off 0.5 carries DC A*(2w-1), and
                                               ;   taking it out leaves the pulse quieter
                                               ;   the narrower it is -- 3.77 dB at 0.12.
                                               ;   The ramp has no such term: rms 1/sqrt(3)
                                               ;   at every width, colour alone.
aosc    = aramp * (1 - kwave) + apuls * kwave

; the DRIVE is a level, and the filter is what it drives.
kpk     = 0.6 * ((1 - kwave) + kwave * 2.36 * max(kdw, 1 - kdw))
                                               ; how tall this wave ALREADY is, from vco2's
                                               ;   own definition rather than from a meter:
                                               ;   the ramp peaks at its amplitude argument
                                               ;   at every width, and the pulse, once the
                                               ;   DC A*(2w-1) two lines up is taken out,
                                               ;   peaks at 2A*max(w,1-w). `kdw` already
                                               ;   carries the age jitter, so this follows
                                               ;   it. The 2.36 is that 2 with vco2's own
                                               ;   band-limiting overshoot on the pulse --
                                               ;   its edges ring past the ideal wave by a
                                               ;   measured 1.18 at width 0.5, against 1.01
                                               ;   on the ramp, which has no edge. Computing
                                               ;   the INPUT a generator needs is arithmetic
                                               ;   on the generator; it is not a fitted
                                               ;   curve laid over its output.
kgmax   = 2.23 / kpk                           ; so the TOP of the knob is the same place
                                               ;   whatever the wave: just under the host's
                                               ;   transparent ceiling (2.523 in body units;
                                               ;   the margin carries `klvl` and vco2's band
                                               ;   limiting overshoot). Where the wave is
                                               ;   already tall there is less room and the
                                               ;   knob gives less -- +11.4 dB on the ramp,
                                               ;   +5.5 on the narrowest pulse -- which is
                                               ;   also what a mixer does. Without this the
                                               ;   pulse generator's upper half met the
                                               ;   scaffold's own hard clip instead of the
                                               ;   ladder: measured p99.9 of 2.92 at width
                                               ;   0.12 and drive 0.67 against a 2.746 wall.
asig    = aosc * (kgmax ^ kdrive) * (1 + klvl) ; even in dB across the knob, which is what a
                                               ;   volume control is. Nothing shapes the wave in
                                               ;   here -- the saturating element is the
                                               ;   synth's LADDER, whose four stages see
                                               ;   whatever level this sends them
                                               ;   (2*Vt*tanh(x/2*Vt), Vt 1.22, so they
                                               ;   bend from about |x| 2.4 up) and which
                                               ;   applies no output compensation on
                                               ;   purpose. Set filter_algorithm to
                                               ;   `ladder` for that; on the svf this knob
                                               ;   is level alone, which is also what an
                                               ;   external input into a clean mixer is.
                                               ; The top is where the host stops being
                                               ;   transparent: this generator peaks 0.617
                                               ;   on the ramp, and 0.617 * 4 = 2.47 sits
                                               ;   just under the scaffold's 2.523. On the
                                               ;   PULSE generator at a narrow width the
                                               ;   wave already peaks 1.28, so there the
                                               ;   last part of the travel meets that
                                               ;   safety clip instead of the ladder --
                                               ;   the same fact as `width`'s own level,
                                               ;   seen from the other end.

Seine Worte zu diesem Eintrag: „ok, abgenommen.“ | „ja, abgenommen, habe ich autorisiert. v. 1.1“ — gehört über tools/lco_listening/analog_osc_params/index.html: 4 Achsen an ihren deklarierten Ankern frei kombinierbar (72 Kombinationen), Kombination durchgehend sichtbar, EIN Pegelfaktor für den Satz, 12 s lange Töne (age wandert mit 0,043 und 0,057 Hz), finetune getrennt als zwei summierte Schichten. Generator: tools/lco_param_page.py.

wave.note: which of the two generators is heard: 0 the ramp one (vco2 imode 4), 1 the pulse one (imode 2), and between them the two are crossfaded. Both read `width` as the same fourth argument, so this control does not name a waveform on its own -- it picks the family and `width` picks the position in it. Measured at 220 Hz with the width at its symmetric 0.5: centroid 675 Hz on the ramp generator (a triangle) against 5620 on the pulse one (a square); at width 0.02 the ramp generator reads 2180 (a saw).

ramp.gloss: the triangle/saw generator -- `width` sets where the ramp breaks

pulse.gloss: the square/pulse generator -- `width` sets the duty

width.note: the fraction of one period spent in the first phase -- rising on the ramp generator, high on the pulse generator -- and it is the same argument to vco2 in both cases. 0.5 is the symmetric one on either: a triangle, a square. There every even harmonic cancels -- odd/even measured 131.3 dB on the ramp generator and 96.5 on the pulse one -- because the amplitudes carry |sin(pi*n*w)| on both (over n on the pulse, over n^2 on the ramp -- the pulse is the derivative of the asymmetric triangle, which is one power of n). Away from 0.5 the even harmonics come in and the nth is cancelled wherever n*w is a whole number. w and 1-w are the same magnitude spectrum, so 0.12 and 0.88 sound alike: measured on the pulse generator with `age` at 0, odd/even 1.6 dB against 1.6 and centroids 4317.1 against 4317.4 Hz. On the PULSE generator a width off 0.5 is also quieter, because the DC it carries, A*(2w-1), is taken out and a narrow pulse is mostly that -- measured 3.77 dB down at 0.12 against 0.5 and 11.28 at 0.02, where rms 2A*sqrt(w(1-w)) predicts 3.74 and 11.06 -- and that is the sound of the thing, not a fault to correct. On the RAMP generator there is no such term: its rms is 1/sqrt(3) at every width -- measured -9.21 dB at 0.02, 0.12, 0.5, 0.88 and 0.98 alike -- so there the same number is colour alone.

end.gloss: the far end: a sawtooth on the ramp generator, a sliver of a pulse on the other

narrow.gloss: well off symmetric -- thin and nasal, and on the pulse generator quieter

symmetric.gloss: odd harmonics only, on either generator: a triangle, a square

wide.gloss: the mirror of narrow -- same spectrum, same level

finetune.note: cents off the played note, so two or three layers of this oscillator can be detuned against each other -- the octave knobs the player has (koct1/2/3) move in octaves and cannot do it. Beating between two layers a few cents apart is what makes a sound thick; that thickness is composed from layers here and is not a knob on one oscillator. Measured: -25 asked gives -25 heard.

flat.gloss: a slow beat against a layer at zero

sharp.gloss: the same beat the other way

drive.note: how hard the oscillator is driven INTO the synth's filter, and nothing else: 0 to 1 is 0 dB up to the loudest this body may be, even in dB across the knob -- +11.4 dB on the ramp generator, +5.5 dB on the narrowest pulse, because that wave is already twice as tall and there is less room above it. There is no shaper in the oscillator. The saturating element is the ladder's own input stage -- the same construction as a Minimoog fed through its External Input Volume, where the mixer runs hot and the filter's transistor stages bend. So this control needs `filter_algorithm` on `ladder` to have its character; on the svf it is level alone, which is what an external input into a clean mixer also is. Measured through this synth's ladder at cutoff 1200, resonance 0.35, 24 dB/oct, filter drive 0: at 110 Hz the output rises 10.70 dB from clean to full, its crest falls 3.17 to 2.45 and its centroid falls 707 to 580 Hz -- the driven sound is darker and denser, not brighter. The reference this was built against (BJ's own Minimoog V External Input Volume recording, 2026-08-01) reads 16.00 dB, crest 2.31 to 1.65, centroid 3253 to 600 Hz, and BJ on its top: 'beim MiniV ist ExtInpVol auch erheblich zu krass'. The top of this knob is instead where the HOST stops being transparent (2.523 in body units), and the body computes how far that is from vco2's own definition of the wave it just made, so the top lands there at every width instead of running into the scaffold's hard clip on the pulse generator.

clean.gloss: unity -- the oscillator as it stands

warm.gloss: a third of the way up, the ladder's stages just starting to bend

hot.gloss: as loud as this body goes -- the filter is being overdriven

age.note: how far the components have drifted: a slow pitch wander, a jitter on the duty, and a slow level wobble, each scaled by this one value and each at its own unrelated rate so they never lock. At 0 the oscillator is mathematically exact and sounds it: that setting is a DCO and not a VCO -- rock-stable digital pitch is the thing a DCO was built to have. Every voice enters the drift at a different phase, so a chord does not wander in lockstep.

dco.gloss: no drift at all. This is what a DCO IS: the pitch comes off a divider rather than out of a VCO's temperature-dependent core, so it does not move. BJ named this anchor (2026-07-30) — a digitally clocked core is exactly this case.

instruments.why: air blown across the mouth of a bottle: a wide, soft, almost noteless tone with only two or three partials over the breath, and it stands as long as it is blown. Built from Csound's waveguide clarinet bore, driven at its blowing pressure (`kamp`) with its upper colour cut back until the tube reads as air over an opening rather than as a reed. NOT the reed instrument (`clarinet`) and not a struck vessel. blow = the pressure: the bore stays closed and hooting over the lower travel and SPEAKS in the top third, where the odd partials come up about 10 dB against the fundamental.
instruments.code:
; LOUDNESS: blow
; `blow` is the blowing PRESSURE on this bore, and pressure carries level with it --
; a bottle blown harder is louder, which is the physics and not an invented envelope.
; Measured at 220 Hz, meter calibrated 88/88, sr 44100: over the map the 3rd partial
; rises 10.1 dB against the fundamental and the crest goes 1.9 -> 4.4 while the rms
; moves 2.05 dB, so colour is what travels. NOT exempted and recorded here rather
; than hidden: the axis and the six registers together still spread 5.74 dB, above
; the 3.00 dB cross-register bound -- 4.11 dB of that is wgclar's own register tilt.
kblow   = 0.55   ; blow [0.00..1.00]: how hard the bottle is blown -- the pressure on the bore, from a closed hoot to as wide open as it goes before it blows out
kpr     = 0.60 + 0.20 * kblow                ; `kamp` IS the blowing pressure on this bore, not
                                             ; an output level. The bore SPEAKS between 0.72 and
                                             ; 0.76: below that the spectrum is frozen, above it
                                             ; the odd partials jump. 0.83 blows the model out of
                                             ; self-oscillation (loudness travel 59 dB), so 0.80
                                             ; is the ceiling and the map stops there.
kdrift  oscili 0.22, 0.07, giSine            ; the air over the mouth is never quite steady
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; `kngain` stays at 0.5. Measured 2026-07-31: over
                                             ; its documented 0..0.5 it is a LEVEL axis and adds
                                             ; no breath at all -- it is not the bore's axis.
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff` and is INERT -- measured
                                             ; bit-identical from -0.9 to 0.0 in this build, so
                                             ; never put a control on it.
                                             ; kvamp is 0: the model's own vibrato stays off.
                                             ; ONE wgclar and no more: a second instance in the
                                             ; same body changes this one -- measured, the 3rd
                                             ; partial of a bore at kamp 0.80 falls from -2.3 to
                                             ; -12.3 dB with an unused second bore beside it.
asig    butterlp asig, kfreq * koct1 * (3.16 * (1 + kdrift))
                                             ; the bore's upper colour cut back until the tube
                                             ; reads as air over an opening and not as a reed;
                                             ; the slow wander on this corner is the body's own
                                             ; movement, and it is coherent where a wander on the
                                             ; pressure was not (it crossed the speaking
                                             ; threshold and read as variance, not motion).
asig    = asig * 1.45 * kvol1
instruments.name: blown bottle

blow.note: the blowing pressure on the bore (`kamp` 0.60..0.80). Measured at 220 Hz, meter calibrated 88/88, sr 44100: the 3rd partial relative to the fundamental goes -12.4 -> -2.3 dB and the 5th -23.5 -> -9.8 dB, the crest 1.9 -> 4.4, while the rms moves 2.05 dB -- a colour axis that carries some level with it, declared `; LOUDNESS: blow`. The change is a THRESHOLD, not a ramp: nothing moves from 0.60 to 0.72 and the bore opens between 0.72 and 0.76. Above 0.80 the model leaves self-oscillation (0.83: loudness travel 59 dB), which is why the map stops there. Not measured at the rate the plugin runs (176400): the harness renders at 44100 and fails its own calibration above that.

hooted.gloss: closed and dull, barely more than the fundamental

at the edge.gloss: the last of the closed tone, just under where it speaks

speaking.gloss: the bore open, the odd partials up about 8 dB

wide open.gloss: as open as the tube goes before it blows out

kdrift  oscili 0.22, 0.07, giSine            ; the air over the mouth is never quite steady
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; `kngain` stays at 0.5. Measured 2026-07-31: over
                                             ; its documented 0..0.5 it is a LEVEL axis and adds
                                             ; no breath at all -- it is not the bore's axis.
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff` and is INERT -- measured
                                             ; bit-identical from -0.9 to 0.0 in this build, so
                                             ; never put a control on it.
                                             ; kvamp is 0: the model's own vibrato stays off.
                                             ; ONE wgclar and no more: a second instance in the
                                             ; same body changes this one -- measured, the 3rd
                                             ; partial of a bore at kamp 0.80 falls from -2.3 to
                                             ; -12.3 dB with an unused second bore beside it.
asig    butterlp asig, kfreq * koct1 * (3.16 * (1 + kdrift))
                                             ; the bore's upper colour cut back until the tube
                                             ; reads as air over an opening and not as a reed;
                                             ; the slow wander on this corner is the body's own
                                             ; movement, and it is coherent where a wander on the
                                             ; pressure was not (it crossed the speaking
                                             ; threshold and read as variance, not motion).
asig    = asig * 1.45 * kvol1

instruments.why: a metal body held ringing by moving air rather than struck: three modes at stretched, non-whole-number spacings, driven continuously by filtered noise whose brightness keeps travelling, so the body never settles and a held note stands. Enigmatic rather than like any named instrument -- machine-room, industrial. Same modal filter bank as `struck_bar` and `cymbal`, but a different body: those are tuned bars and cymbals with whole-number-ish or dense spacings, this one is deliberately stretched and its character comes from the drive moving. stretch = from a hollow whole-number tube to a wide stretched bell. drive = how bright the air working the body is.
instruments.code:
kstr    = 0.475                             ; how far the modes are stretched off whole numbers
kr2     = 2.00 + 1.60 * kstr
kr3     = 3.00 + 5.20 * kstr
kdrv    = 0.40                              ; how bright the air driving the body is
kcen    = 600 * (11.667 ^ kdrv)
aexc    rand 0.05
kcut    oscili kcen * 0.35, 0.09, giSine     ; the drive keeps moving, so the body keeps changing
kcut    = kcen + kcut
aexc    butterlp aexc, kcut
a1      mode aexc, kfreq * koct1, 340        ; three modes, driven CONTINUOUSLY rather than struck:
a2      mode aexc, kfreq * koct1 * kr2, 260  ;   a held note stands, and the host owns the note-off
a3      mode aexc, kfreq * koct1 * kr3, 190
asig    = (a1 * 0.6 + a2 * 0.3 + a3 * 0.16) * 0.27
asig    = asig * kvol1
instruments.name: driven metal

stretch.note: how far the two upper modes sit off whole-number multiples of the played pitch. at zero they are the 2nd and 3rd harmonic and the body reads as a hollow tube with a note; stretched, the spacings go wide and it reads as a bell or a plate with no clear note. measured: centroid 363 -> 532 Hz across the axis with the loudness holding inside 0.2 dB. both ratios are k-rate, so the stretch may travel over the note.

tube.gloss: whole-number spacings: hollow, with a clear note

bell.gloss: the found body: wide, metallic, no settled note

plate.gloss: far stretched: a plate, all clang and no pitch

drive.note: how bright the air driving the body is, which decides how much of the upper modes ever get woken. measured: centroid 349 -> 526 Hz with the loudness inside 0.2 dB. do NOT reach for the modes' Q instead -- measured over Q 60..1400 that is a 12.3 dB loudness ramp for 56 Hz of colour, i.e. a volume fader wearing a timbre name.

muffled.gloss: worked by dull air; only the lowest mode speaks

room.gloss: the found drive: a machine room

bright.gloss: brighter air, the upper modes come up

hissing.gloss: driven by full-band hiss, all modes lit
